Once upon a time, there was a pretty little girl called Julie who liked to run. She ran all around the garden, in and out of the trees, over the bridge and around the lake. 

One day, Julie was running around the lake when she noticed a door at the edge with a sign saying "Exit". She had never seen this door before and she wanted to open it. 

So Julie ran up to the door and tried to open it, but it was shut tight. She shouted out loudly, "Please let me in!" 

A voice came from the other side of the door, "No! You must not open this door, it is not safe for you!" 

Julie continued to ask to be let in, but the voice kept saying "No". Finally, Julie realised she must not open the door, as she could get hurt. 

So instead of trying to open the door, she decided to run around the lake again, enjoying the pretty view and the sunshine. 

This story teaches us that we should always listen to adults when they tell us something that might be dangerous. We should not take risks like trying to open doors if we don't know what is on the other side.

One day, he was walking through the jungle when he spotted a bow on the ground made of the brightest ribbon. Curious, he stopped to investigate and discovered it was a gift that a little bird had left for him! The tiger was so excited and immediately began tying bows using the ribbon gift.

But soon he realized someone else wanted the ribbon too. It was a small rabbit who was looking for a way to decorate her burrow. The tiger and the rabbit got into an argument over who should get the ribbon. The tiger felt like he deserved it since it was his ribbon gift, but the rabbit felt like she deserved it since she had been looking for it for so long.

The tiger was about to take the ribbon for himself when he realized that the right thing to do was share the ribbon with the rabbit so both of them could be happy. And so the tiger helped the happy rabbit with her decorations, and from that day forward, they became friends.

The moral of the story is that when you share with others, everyone can be happy. Being tidy and tying bows are one thing, but the most important thing is to be kind to those around you.

Jill and Tom were friends who liked to play with books. They liked to look at the pictures and try to say the words. One day, they found a big book with many strange words. They did not know what the words meant, but they thought they were funny.

They decided to play a game. They would pick a word and try to spell it with the letters they had. They would take turns and laugh at each other's mistakes. They did not care if they spelled the words right or wrong. They just wanted to have fun.

But one word was not like the others. It was a very long word with many letters. It was orange and had a star on it. Jill and Tom did not know what it was, but they thought it was the best word. They wanted to spell it and see what would happen.

Jill went first. She took the letters and tried to spell the word. She did not have enough letters, so she used some from other words. She did not know she was making a big mistake. She spelled the word wrong and said it out loud.

Suddenly, the book glowed and made a loud noise. A bright light came out of the book and hit Jill. She screamed and fell to the floor. She was not Jill anymore. She was a frog.

Tom was scared and ran away. He left the book and Jill behind. He did not help his friend. He did not say sorry. He just wanted to be safe.

The book was still glowing and making noise. It was angry. It did not like what Jill and Tom did. It did not like that they played with the words and did not respect them. It did not like that they laughed at the words and did not learn from them. It did not like that Tom left Jill and did not care for her.

The book wanted to teach them a lesson. It wanted them to know that words are powerful and important. It wanted them to know that words can be good or bad, depending on how they are used. It wanted them to know that words can make or break friendships, depending on how they are said.

The book opened and showed another word. It was a very short word with two letters. It was green and had a heart on it. It was the only word that could help Jill. It was the word "if".

But Tom did not see the word. He did not come back to the book. He did not try to spell the word. He did not say the word. He did not save his friend.

Jill was stuck as a frog. She could not talk or play or laugh. She could only hop and croak and cry. She missed Tom and the books and the words. She wished he would come back and say sorry and spell the word. She wished he would be her friend again.

But he did not.

The end.

Moral: Words are powerful and important. Use them wisely and kindly. Respect them and learn from them. Do not play with them or laugh at them. Do not hurt your friends with them or leave them behind. Say sorry and spell "if" when you make a mistake. Be a good friend.

Uncle Tom smiles and says, "It is a surprise for you, Emma. Do you want to see it?"

Emma nods and says, "Yes, please, uncle Tom. Can I open it?"

Uncle Tom says, "Of course, you can, Emma. But first, you have to do something for me. You have to let me wear your purple hat."

Emma giggles and says, "Okay, uncle Tom. You can wear my purple hat. But it is very small for you."

She takes off her purple hat and puts it on uncle Tom's head. It looks funny and silly. Emma and her mom laugh. Uncle Tom laughs too.

He says, "Thank you, Emma. You are very sweet. Now you can open the box."

Emma opens the box and sees a beautiful purple dress. It has flowers and ribbons on it. It is the prettiest dress she has ever seen.

She says, "Wow, uncle Tom. It is a purple dress. I love it. Thank you, thank you, thank you."

She hugs uncle Tom and gives him a kiss. He hugs her back and says, "You are very welcome, Emma. I am glad you like it. You can try it on if you want."

Emma says, "Yes, I want to try it on. Can you help me, mom?"

Mom says, "Sure, Emma. Let's go to your room and put on your purple dress. You will look like a princess."

Emma and her mom go to her room. Uncle Tom follows them. He takes off his purple hat and puts it back on Emma's head. He says, "You can keep my purple hat, Emma. It looks better on you."

Emma says, "Thank you, uncle Tom. You are the best uncle ever."

She smiles and twirls in her purple dress. She feels happy and loved.

"Maybe we should let it go," Tom says.

"Yeah, it is not nice to keep it in the net," Sam says.

"Bye, frog!" Tom and Sam say.

"Ribbit, ribbit!" the frog says.

Tom and Sam smile and wave. They are glad they did the right thing. They still like to play with their net, but they only catch bugs and fish that they can put back. They are kind to the animals in the pond.

Tim went back home and enjoyed his cereal. He knew that when his cereal box was empty, he could always ask his friends for help. From that day on, Tim and Sue became best friends and shared many things with each other. And they always had fun eating cereal together.

In the end, the bird and the dog stopped fighting. They decided to share the beautiful glass. The bird could have it for its nest, and the dog could play with it when the bird was not using it. They became friends and were happy to share the pretty glass.

They found the feather near the big tree. The bird was very happy and thanked the squirrel. The squirrel was happy to help the honest bird. From that day, the bird and the squirrel became best friends and played together without disturbing anyone.

One day, a strong bear named Bobo went to the store. He wanted to weigh a big box. The box was very heavy. He asked his friend, a little bird named Toto, to help him.

"Can you help me weigh this box, Toto?" asked Bobo. Toto said, "Yes, I can help you!" They both tried to lift the box, but it was too heavy. They decided to take it home and try again.

At home, they tried to weigh the box again. This time, they lifted it up high. But, oh no! The box hit the ceiling and made a big hole. The ceiling started to crack. Bobo and Toto were scared.

They tried to fix the hole, but it was too big. The ceiling fell down on the box. Bobo and Toto were very sad. They could not fix their home.

After the race, Tim and his mom counted the rocks. Tim had found 20 rocks! His mom gave him a big trophy. Tim was so happy. He put the trophy next to his bed and looked at it every night before he went to sleep. The end.

When he got back to his friends, he told them about the scary monster. They all laughed and said he was just imagining things. But Floppy knew what he saw. 

Later that day, Floppy and his friends were playing a game of hide-and-seek. Floppy found the perfect hiding spot behind a big rock. But when he peeked out, he saw the scary monster again! This time, the monster was coming right towards him. Floppy tried to run, but it was too late. The monster caught him and took him away. 

From that day on, Floppy's friends always listened to him when he was scared. They never forgot the scary monster that took their friend away.

They measured out the batter and put it in the oven. Soon, the cupcakes were done and they snuggled up together, enjoying the warm treats and a good story.

In the end, the farmer decided to share his flowers with everyone in the village. The villagers were happy and grateful for the farmer's kindness. The moral of the story is that being kind and fair is more important than being wealthy.

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Lily. She loved to eat popcorn, especially the green ones. One day, she asked her mom to make some popcorn for her. Her mom said yes and started making it.

As the popcorn was popping in the pot, Lily saw a bug crawling on the floor. She was scared of bugs and didn't want it to come near her popcorn. So, she tried to roll the popcorn bowl away from the bug, but it was too heavy for her.

Lily's mom saw her struggling and came to help. She picked up the bowl and moved it away from the bug. Then, she explained to Lily that bugs are harmless and we should never be afraid of them. Lily learned that it's important to be brave and not let fear get in the way of enjoying something she loves, like her green popcorn. From that day on, Lily never let bugs scare her again.

"Sure!" Lily said. "But let's add some more toys to make it more fun!" 

So they added some blocks and cars to the mix. They played for a while, but then Timmy accidentally knocked over one of the dolls. 

"Oh no!" Lily said. "You broke my doll!" 

"I'm sorry," Timmy said. "Can you fix it?" 

Lily looked at the doll and saw that its head was a little soft. She judged that it could be fixed. 

"It's okay," she said. "I can fix it. Let's get some tape." 

They found some tape and Lily fixed the doll. They continued playing and had a great time together. The end.

"Let's make a card for Mom while the cake bakes," Lily said. She got some paper, crayons, and stickers. Ben got some scissors and glue. They sat on the floor and started to draw and cut.

Suddenly, they saw a line of ants on the floor. The ants were going to the bowl where they had left some batter. "Oh no, the ants are eating our cake mix!" Ben cried. He tried to shoo them away with his hand, but they kept coming.

Lily had an idea. She grabbed the glue bottle and squeezed some glue on the floor. The glue was sticky and wet. The ants got stuck in the glue and could not move. "Ha, we got them!" Lily said. She smiled at Ben.

But then they heard a loud noise from the oven. They ran to the kitchen and saw smoke coming out. The cake had risen too much and broken the oven door. The cake was burned and black. "Oh no, our cake is broken!" Lily cried. She looked at Ben.

They both felt sad. They had no cake and no card for Mom. They had ants and glue on the floor and smoke in the air. They hugged each other and started to cry.

"Here you go, Lily, you can have the cheese sandwich and the tomato soup. And Ben, you can have the ham sandwich and the chicken soup." Mom said, putting the food on their plates and bowls.

"Thank you, Mom!" Lily and Ben said, picking up their forks and spoons.

They started to eat. They liked the sandwiches. They were soft and tasty. But when they tried the soup, they made a funny face. The soup was hot and spicy. It burned their tongues and made them cough.

"Mom, this soup is spicy!" Lily said, putting down her spoon.

"Mom, this soup is spicy!" Ben said, putting down his spoon.

Mom looked at them and realized her mistake. She had mixed up the soups. She had given them the spicy soup that Dad liked, and kept the mild soup for herself.

"Oh, I'm sorry, kids, I gave you the wrong soup!" Mom said, feeling bad. "I didn't mean to. I was in a hurry and I didn't check the labels. Here, let me switch them for you."

She took the bowls and gave them the right soup. She also gave them some water and milk to cool their mouths.

"Is this better?" Mom asked, hoping they would forgive her.

"Yes, Mom, this soup is good!" Lily said, taking a sip.

"Yes, Mom, this soup is good!" Ben said, taking a sip.

They smiled and finished their lunch. They were happy again. Mom was happy too. She hugged them and kissed them.

"I'm glad you like the soup, kids. I love you very much. You are my best display of love." Mom said, making them giggle.

They hugged her back and said, "We love you too, Mom. You are our best display of love too."

The big dog is surprised. He does not want to fight Rex. He runs away from the woods. He does not come back.

Tom and Sam were playing on the beach. They made a big sand castle with a flag and a moat. They were very proud of their castle.

But then the tide came in. The water got closer and closer to their castle. Tom and Sam tried to stop it. They dug a trench and piled up more sand. But the water was too strong. It broke their trench and filled their moat. It reached their castle walls.

"Help! Help!" Tom and Sam shouted. "Our castle is going to fall!"

A man heard them and came over. He was wearing a hat and a coat. He had a big smile.

"Hello, boys," he said. "What's the matter?"

"The water is taking our castle!" Tom and Sam cried. "We worked so hard on it!"

The man nodded. He looked at the water and the castle. He said, "I see. That's a very nice castle. But you know, the water always wins. It's part of nature. You can't fight it. You have to surrender."

"Surrender?" Tom and Sam asked. They did not like that word. It sounded like giving up.

"Yes, surrender," the man said. "It means to let go. To accept what is. To find something else to do. Maybe you can make a boat or a fish or a starfish. There are many things you can do with sand and water. But you can't stop the tide."

Tom and Sam looked at each other. They felt hurt. They loved their castle. They did not want to let it go. But they also saw that the man was right. The water was not going to stop. Their castle was going to fall.

They sighed. They took their flag and their bucket and their shovel. They said goodbye to their castle. They said, "Thank you, water, for letting us play. We surrender."

They followed the man to a new spot on the beach. He helped them make a boat and a fish and a starfish. They had fun. They learned something new. They forgot about their castle. They were happy.

Lila was a dog who liked to play with her friends in the park. She ran, jumped and barked with joy. But one day, she felt something itchy on her fur. She scratched and scratched, but it did not help. She looked at her fur and saw a tiny bug. It was a flea!

Lila was scared of the flea. She thought it would bite her and make her sick. She ran away from her friends and hid under a bench. She hoped the flea would go away.

But the flea did not go away. It jumped from Lila's fur to the fur of another dog. The dog was Rex, Lila's best friend. Rex felt the flea and started to scratch. He was angry and confused. He did not know where the flea came from.

He saw Lila under the bench. He walked towards her and asked, "Lila, did you give me this flea? Why did you do that?"

Lila felt guilty. She knew she had given Rex the flea. She did not mean to do that. She was sorry. She came out from under the bench and looked at Rex. She said, "Rex, I am sorry. I did not know I had a flea. I was scared and I ran away. I did not want to hurt you."

Rex saw Lila's sad eyes. He knew she was telling the truth. He was not angry anymore. He said, "Lila, it's okay. I forgive you. You are my friend. We can go to the vet and get rid of the flea. Come on, let's go."

Lila was happy. She wagged her tail and licked Rex's face. She said, "Thank you, Rex. You are a good friend. I am sorry again."

Rex smiled and said, "You're welcome, Lila. Don't worry. Let's go."

They walked together to the vet. They passed by their other friends in the park. They said hello and bowed to them. They did not tell them about the flea. They wanted to keep it a secret. They were happy and relieved. They hoped they would never see a flea again.

"Thank you, Mr. Lee! You are the best!" they said.

"You're welcome, kids. I'm glad I could help. But remember, you should always take good care of your things and not break them on purpose. And if you need help, you should always be polite and grateful to those who help you. That's how you make friends and show respect." Mr. Lee said.

Tom and Lily nodded and thanked him again. They learned a valuable lesson that day. They hugged each other and played with their wagon happily. They also shared their toys, books, and snacks with Mr. Lee, who joined them for a while. They had a lot of fun and made a new friend.

One day, a young prince went to the park with his mother. He saw a big pond with many ducks and fish. He wanted to feed them some bread, so he asked his mother for some.

"Here you are, my dear," his mother said, giving him a slice of bread. "But be careful not to fall into the water. It is very deep and cold."

The young prince nodded and ran to the edge of the pond. He tore the bread into small pieces and threw them to the ducks and fish. They came closer and closer, quacking and splashing. The young prince laughed and clapped his hands. He was having so much fun.

But he did not notice that he was leaning too far over the water. Suddenly, he lost his balance and slipped. He fell into the pond with a splash. He felt the water fill his mouth and nose. He was scared and cold. He tried to swim, but he did not know how.

"Help! Help!" he cried. "I can't breathe!"

His mother heard his cry and ran to the pond. She saw him struggling in the water. She was very worried and scared. She jumped into the pond and grabbed him. She pulled him out of the water and hugged him.

"Are you all right, my dear?" she asked, checking him for injuries. "You gave me such a fright!"

The young prince coughed and spat out some water. He was shivering and wet. He felt sorry and ashamed.

"I'm sorry, mother," he said. "I was too careless. I wanted to feed the ducks and fish, but I fell into the water. I was so scared. I thought I was going to die."

His mother kissed him and comforted him.

"It's all right, my dear," she said. "You are safe now. I'm glad you are not hurt. But you must be more careful next time. The water is not for drinking, it is for the ducks and fish. You are not a duck or a fish, you are a young prince. And young princes need to drink milk and juice, not water from the pond."

The young prince nodded and smiled. He learned his lesson. He never went too close to the water again. He still liked to feed the ducks and fish, but he always stayed with his mother. And he always drank his milk and juice, like a good young prince.

"Hello, bear," said Lily. "You look different. What kind of bear are you?"

"I am a grizzly bear," replied the bear. "I suggest you be careful around me. I may look different, but I am still a wild animal."

Lily nodded her head and said, "I understand. I will be careful." She continued on her walk, but she couldn't stop thinking about the bear. She wondered if all bears were different from each other, just like people. 

As she walked back home, she saw her mom and told her about the bear. "Mom, I met a grizzly bear today. He looked different from other bears."

Her mom smiled and said, "Yes, bears can be different just like people. But remember, bears are wild animals and we should always be careful around them." 

Lily nodded her head and said, "I will remember that, Mom." And she went to bed that night dreaming of all the different kinds of bears she might meet one day.

One day, Tom's friend, a little mouse named Jerry, came to visit. Jerry saw the thermometer and wanted to play with it too. Tom said, "No, it's mine! You can't play with it!" Jerry felt sad and asked, "Why can't we share the thermometer and play together?"

Tom thought about it and decided to share his toy with Jerry. They both played with the thermometer and had a lot of fun. But suddenly, the thermometer disappeared! Tom and Jerry looked everywhere for it, but they could not find it. They were both very sad.

Later, Tom's mom found the thermometer and gave it back to them. Tom and Jerry were very happy. They learned that sharing can make them happy and that being grumpy and not sharing can make things disappear. From that day on, Tom was not grumpy anymore, and they both shared their toys and played happily together.

Lily was very sad and started to cry. Her big brother tried to help her find the teddy bear, but they still couldn't find it. Suddenly, Lily had an idea. She remembered that sometimes when she was sad, her mommy would give her a big hug and squeeze her tight. So, she thought maybe if she squeezed her pillow tight, it would make her feel better.

Lily squeezed her pillow so hard that it burst open and feathers flew everywhere. She was so surprised that she fell off her bed and hit her head. She had to go to the hospital and get stitches. When she got home, she found her teddy bear under her bed. But, Lily learned that sometimes squeezing things too hard can lead to bad things happening.

Once upon a time, in a big jungle, there was a beautiful tiger. The tiger had a lot of friends. They liked to play and have fun together. One day, they saw a big tree with a lot of fruit. They all wanted the fruit, but they did not know how to get it.

A small bird saw them and said, "I can help you get the fruit. All you need to do is clap your paws and the fruit will fall down." The tiger and his friends were very happy. They all started to clap their paws. But the fruit did not fall down.

The beautiful tiger was sad. He thought his friends were mad at him. But his friends said, "Don't worry, we can try again." They all clapped their paws one more time. This time, the fruit fell down from the tree. The tiger and his friends were very happy. They ate the fruit and played together all day.

One day, a big dog and a little cat were playing near a fountain. The big dog saw the water in the fountain and said, "I want to drink from the fountain."

The little cat said, "I want to drink too, but I am too small to reach the water."

The big dog thought for a moment, then he bowed down and let the little cat climb onto his back. The little cat was now able to drink from the fountain. The little cat said, "Thank you, big dog!"

A bird was watching them and felt envious. The bird said, "Why can't I have a friend like the big dog?"

The big dog and the little cat heard the bird and said, "You can be our friend too! We can all share and help each other."

The moral of the story is: It is good to help others and share what you have.

Then, something happened. Tim saw a smaller tree. He thought it would be enough wood for his mom. The squirrel was happy that Tim did not cut his home. Tim got the wood for his mom, and they all enjoyed the delicious cake.

Just then, Timmy's mom came outside and saw him looking sad. She asked him what was wrong and he told her about the crazy squirrel. His mom told him not to worry, they could try to catch the squirrel together another day. Timmy felt better and went back to playing on the ground with his toys.

But when Timmy went to get his toy car, he couldn't find it. He looked everywhere, but it was nowhere to be found. Timmy was sad and didn't know what to do. Billy asked, "What's wrong, Timmy?" Timmy replied, "I can't find my green car. I don't know where it is."

Billy said, "Let's use my red car instead. It's just as fun." Timmy was hesitant at first, but he decided to give it a try. They played with the red car for a while and had a lot of fun. But when they were done playing, they found Timmy's green car under the couch. Timmy was happy to have found his toy car, but he realized that using Billy's red car was a good result too.

Once upon a time, a small boy named Derek began his journey. He was excited for a fresh start and as he walked on the dusty road, his shoes made scuffing sounds in the dirt and he laughed with joy. 

As Derek kept walking, he soon came across some muddy puddles. He thought it was great fun and wiggled his toes in the filthy water. Suddenly, a passerby stopped him and said, "What are you doing in that dirty water boy? You must be careful, troubles lurk in places like this!"

Derek stood up and realized how right the man was. He thanked him, waved goodbye and continued on his journey with more caution than before. 

This taught Derek a valuable lesson: while it can be fun to explore, it is important to stay safe and watch out for trouble. That day, Derek had an extra special journey, learning to be a responsible little boy.

Jill put the cheese back on the table and started to cry. 

"But I was hungry," said Jill.

Her father took a deep breath. He said, "It's okay. Why don't you watch me make you a cheese sandwich?"

Nana was taking her Grandson, Billy, for a walk. As they walked, Billy asked Nana "Why is this road so old?". Nana looked down at him with a smile and said "Well, Billy, this road is old because it has been here a long, long time. It is one of the oldest roads around here."

Billy stopped and asked Nana, "What's been living on this road all this time?". Nana laughed and said, "Well, Billy, lots of things. But mostly birds, squirrels and people."

Billy looked around and pointed to the stream running alongside the road. Nana bent down and said, "Look, Billy, do you see that stream? It is called a creek. But do you see how it isn't moving? We need to stir it up so it can keep moving down the road!"

Nana grabbed a stick and carefully stirred up the creek until the water began to flow again. Billy cheered and clapped as the water moved down the road.

Nana smiled at her Grandson. It was a moment she would always remember.

Once upon a time, there was a young bee named Buzz. Buzz searched all over for some honey to eat. He buzzed around and soon found an old tree. With its branches, it was the perfect place to find honey.

Buzz flew into the tree and started to look around. He crawled up the branches, crossed over the leaves and hopped around. He soon discovered a whole hive of honey! He quickly filled his tummy and flew away.

On the way back to his hive, he stopped to take a rest. While he was resting, he saw another young bee buzzing around.

Buzz shouted, "Hey, young bee! Come with me! I've found some honey for us both to share!"

The young bee was so excited that he flew over to Buzz. They shared the honey, ate as much as they wanted and flew off together.

They drank the sweet honey and Buzz said, "It's important to grow. So come with me and we can grow together!"

The young bee was happy and followed Buzz on his journey. As they flew together they grew bigger and stronger.

One day, Tommy was walking down the street. He was feeling very impatient and wanted to go home and eat dinner. Suddenly, Tommy heard a strange sound coming from ahead. He followed the sound and came across an old green car, parked in the corner of the street. The car was whistling, with a light coming from the inside.

Tommy curiously stepped closer and saw an old man sitting inside. The old man smiled and asked Tommy why he was so impatient. Tommy, who had never met an old man before, didn't know how to answer.

The old man laughed and said, "It's okay, little one. Do you want to sit in the car and whistle with me?"

Tommy happily accepted the offer and climbed in the car. The old man and Tommy both began to whistle together. The little light in the car became brighter and brighter as they whistled along, until it was the brightest light in the whole street. 

Tommy and the old man stopped and smiled at each other. Tommy couldn't believe his luck, and said, "Can I come and whistle with you again tomorrow?"

The old man agreed, and Tommy went on his way, with a smile on his face.

But then it started to rain. The rain was very heavy and loud. Ben and Mia ran inside the house. They did not want to get wet. But Spot did not follow them. He stayed outside and played with the ball. He did not mind the rain. He liked to get wet.

After a while, the rain stopped. Ben and Mia looked out of the window. They saw Spot lying on the grass. He was very wet and dirty. His fur was all muddy and sticky. He looked terrible.

"Spot, come here!" Ben called. "You need a bath!"

Spot heard Ben and ran to the door. He wagged his tail and barked. He wanted to go inside and see Ben and Mia.

But when he got to the door, Ben and Mia did not let him in. They said, "No, Spot, you are too wet and dirty. You have to stay outside until you are dry and clean."

Spot did not understand. He felt sad and confused. He did not like to be outside alone. He did not like to be wet and dirty. He wanted to be inside with Ben and Mia. He wanted to be dry and clean.

He whined and scratched at the door. He hoped that Ben and Mia would change their minds and let him in. He did not know what to do. He wished that the rain had never come. He wished that he had followed Ben and Mia inside. He wished that he had not played with the ball. He wished that his fur was not terrible.

Lila liked to whistle. She whistled when she played, when she ate, and when she went to bed. She whistled all kinds of songs, from happy ones to sad ones. She whistled so much that her mom and dad sometimes asked her to stop.

One day, Lila found a big wall in the park. It was very tall and long and had many colors on it. Lila thought it was pretty. She wanted to whistle a song for the wall. She walked up to the wall and opened her mouth. But no sound came out. She tried again and again, but nothing happened. She felt sad and confused.

"Hello, little girl," a voice said. Lila looked around, but she saw no one. "Who are you?" she asked. "I am the wall," the voice said. "I can talk to you, but you can't whistle to me." Lila was surprised and scared. "Why not?" she asked. "Because I have a deep secret," the wall said. "A secret that only I know. And if you whistle to me, you might find out my secret. And I don't want that."

Lila was curious and brave. She wanted to know the wall's secret. She thought it might be something fun or nice. She decided to whistle to the wall anyway. She took a deep breath and whistled as loud as she could. She whistled a song that she liked a lot. She waited for the wall to say something.

But the wall did not say anything. Instead, it started to shake and crack. Lila heard a loud noise and saw a big hole in the wall. She saw something shiny and bright inside the hole. She wondered what it was. She took a step closer to the hole. But then she heard her mom calling her name. She turned around and saw her mom running towards her. She looked worried and angry.

"Lila, what did you do?" her mom asked. "You broke the wall! You can't do that! That's bad! Come here, right now!" Lila felt sorry and scared. She did not mean to break the wall. She did not know it had a secret. She wanted to see what was inside the hole. But she also wanted to go to her mom. She did not know what to do. She wished she had not whistled to the wall.

Anna and Ben were twins who liked to play together. They had a big house with a fireplace and a chimney. Sometimes, they pretended to be Santa and his helpers and put toys in a big bag.

One day, they decided to play Santa and his helpers again. They put on red hats and coats and filled the bag with their stuffed animals. Anna said, "I will be Santa and you will be my helper, Ben. We will go down the chimney and give toys to the children."

Ben nodded and followed Anna to the fireplace. They climbed on a chair and looked at the chimney. It was dark and narrow. Anna said, "Are you ready, Ben? We have to be very quiet and careful."

Ben said, "Yes, I am ready, Anna. But how will we go down the chimney? It is too small for us."

Anna said, "We will use magic, Ben. We will say a magic word and we will become very small. Then we will slide down the chimney. The magic word is 'name'. Can you say it with me?"

Ben said, "Yes, I can say it with you, Anna. Name, name, name!"

They said the magic word three times and felt themselves shrinking. They became as small as mice and fit in the chimney. They held the bag and slid down the chimney. They landed on a soft rug in front of the fireplace. They saw a big tree with lights and ornaments and a lot of presents under it.

Anna said, "Wow, this is a beautiful house, Ben. Look at all the presents. We have to find the ones with our names on them and put our toys next to them."

Ben said, "OK, Anna. Let's look for our names. I see mine. It is on a big box. What is in it, I wonder?"

Anna said, "I see mine too. It is on a small box. Maybe it is a necklace or a ring. Let's open them and see."

They opened their presents and found out what was in them. Anna got a necklace with a heart pendant and Ben got a remote-controlled car. They were very happy and hugged each other.

Anna said, "Thank you, Santa, for these wonderful gifts. We love them. And thank you, Ben, for being my helper. You are the best brother ever."

Ben said, "Thank you, Santa, for these amazing gifts. We love them. And thank you, Anna, for being Santa. You are the best sister ever."

They put their toys next to their presents and climbed back up the chimney. They said the magic word again and became big again. They jumped off the chair and ran to their room. They put on their pajamas and snuggled in their beds. They felt very comfortable and sleepy.

Anna said, "Good night, Ben. I had a lot of fun today. Did you?"

Ben said, "Good night, Anna. I had a lot of fun too. You are a great Santa."

They closed their eyes and dreamed of their toys and their magic adventure.

One day, her mom said, "Lily, we need to go to the shop and buy some food. Do you want to come with me?" Lily shook her head and said, "No, mom, I want to stay here with my stuff." Her mom said, "Okay, but you will miss something fun. I will be back soon."

Lily stayed at home and played with her stuff. She made a tea party for her dolls and read a book to them. She was happy and quiet.

Lily and Ben were playing in the kitchen. They liked to pretend they were chefs and make yummy food. Lily saw a big cabinet with a shiny lock. She wondered what was inside.

"Ben, look at that cabinet. Do you think there are treats in there?" she asked.

Ben shrugged. He was busy stirring a pot of water and salt. "I don't know. Maybe. But we can't open it. Mom said it's not for us."

Lily felt curious. She wanted to see what was in the cabinet. She climbed on a chair and reached for the lock. She pulled and twisted, but it did not open.

"Stop it, Lily. You'll get in trouble. Mom said to trust her. She knows what's best for us." Ben said.

Lily did not listen. She kept trying to open the lock. She thought she was brilliant and could figure it out. She did not notice that Mom was coming back from the store.

Suddenly, the lock clicked and the cabinet opened. Lily gasped. She saw a lot of bottles and cans with colorful labels. They looked like juice and soda. She grabbed one and opened it.

"Wow, this smells good. I want to try it." she said.

She took a sip and made a face. It was not juice or soda. It was something bitter and strong. It burned her mouth and throat. She coughed and spit it out.

"Yuck! What is this?" she cried.

Mom heard the noise and rushed to the kitchen. She saw Lily with the bottle and the open cabinet. She was angry and scared.

"Lily, what have you done? That's not for you. That's alcohol. It's very bad for you. You could get sick or hurt. Why didn't you trust me?" she said.

Lily felt sorry and ashamed. She dropped the bottle and ran to Mom. She hugged her and said.

"I'm sorry, Mom. I was curious. I wanted to see what was in the cabinet. I didn't trust you. I was not brilliant. I was silly. Please forgive me."

Mom hugged her back and said.

"I forgive you, Lily. But you have to promise me to never do that again. You have to trust me. I love you and I want you to be safe and healthy. OK?"

Lily nodded and said.

"OK, Mom. I love you too. And I trust you."

Mom smiled and said.

"Good. Now let's go and wash your mouth. And then we can have some real juice and cookies. How does that sound?"

Lily smiled and said.

"That sounds great, Mom. Thank you."

They left the kitchen and went to the bathroom. Ben followed them. He was glad that Lily was OK. He hoped she learned her lesson. He also hoped that Mom would not forget about his pot of water and salt. He still wanted to be a chef.

Tom and Sam were brothers who liked to go to the lake with their dad. Their dad was a fisherman who knew how to catch many fish. He taught Tom and Sam how to use a rod and a hook and a worm. They had fun watching the fish swim and bite.

One day, they went to the lake and saw a lively duck. The duck was quacking and splashing and flapping its wings. Tom and Sam wanted to play with the duck, so they threw some bread crumbs into the water. The duck came closer and ate the bread. Tom and Sam laughed and clapped.

But then, something bad happened. The duck saw the worm on Sam's hook and thought it was food. It snapped at the worm and got caught on the hook. The duck started to cry and struggle. Sam felt a tug on his rod and pulled. He saw the duck and was scared. He did not want to hurt the duck.

"Dad, dad, help!" Sam shouted. "I caught a duck!"

Their dad heard Sam and ran to him. He saw the duck and the hook and was calm. He took the rod from Sam and gently reeled in the duck. He held the duck in his hands and carefully removed the hook from its beak. He checked the duck for injuries and found none. He stroked the duck's feathers and spoke softly.

"It's okay, little duck. You are not hurt. You are free. Go back to your friends. And be careful next time. Worms are not for ducks. They are for fish."

He let go of the duck and watched it fly away. The duck quacked once and then joined the other ducks on the lake. Tom and Sam saw the duck and felt happy. They hugged their dad and thanked him.

"Thank you, dad. You are a good fisherman and a good duck saver."

Their dad smiled and hugged them back.

"You are welcome, boys. You are good sons and good fishermen too. But remember, fishing is not a game. You have to be respectful of the animals and the nature. And sometimes, you have to let go of what you catch."

They nodded and agreed. They learned a lesson that day. They still liked to fish, but they also liked to watch the ducks and feed them bread. They never caught a duck again.

"What is this?" Lila asked.

"I don't know. Let's look inside," Ben said.

"Wow, these are cool," Ben said. He picked up one of the shiny things and held it in his hand. It was warm and smooth. He rubbed it and it started to glow.

"Look, Lila, it's glowing!" Ben said.

Lila came closer and saw the shiny thing. It was glowing blue and green and red. She reached out to touch it, but Ben pulled it away.

"No, it's mine. I found it first," Ben said.

"That's not fair. I want to see it too," Lila said.

They started to argue and tug at the shiny thing. They did not notice that the shiny thing was making noises. It was saying something in a language they did not understand.

"Stop, stop, stop!" the shiny thing said.

Lila and Ben stopped and looked at the shiny thing. It was still glowing and talking.

"Who are you?" Lila asked.

"I am a star. I came from the sky. I was in a book, but someone took me out. I want to go back," the shiny thing said.

"A star? You are a star?" Ben asked.

"Yes, I am a star. And you are silly. You should not fight over me. You should share and be nice," the shiny thing said.

Lila and Ben felt sorry. They did not mean to be silly. They did not mean to hurt the star.

"We are sorry, star. We did not know you were alive. We will share and be nice. Can we be your friends?" Lila asked.

Tom felt his face get hot. He closed his book and said, "Um, it's a mystery book. It's about a detective."

Lily nodded and said, "I like mystery books too. They are fun and exciting. Do you want to play with me? We can pretend to be detectives and look for clues in the playground."

Tom was surprised. He did not expect Lily to offer to play with him. He felt nervous, but also curious. He wanted to play with Lily and be her friend.

He opened his book again and showed her a picture of the detective and his magnifying glass. He said, "Okay, let's play. I have a magnifying glass too. It's in my backpack. We can use it to find clues."

Lily smiled and said, "Great! Let's go then. Maybe we can solve a mystery together."

Tom put his book and his magnifying glass in his backpack and followed Lily to the playground. He felt happy and brave. He was not shy anymore. He had a new friend who liked mystery books too.

Lily was a rabbit who loved carrots. She liked to eat them every day. She had a garden where she grew many carrots. They were long and orange and crunchy.

One day, she saw a big truck stop near her garden. A man got out of the truck. He had a big bag and a shovel. He walked to Lily's garden and started to dig up her carrots. He put them in his bag.

Lily was very angry. She ran to the man and said, "Stop! Those are my carrots! You are stealing them!"

The man did not listen. He said, "I don't care. I need these carrots for my soup. Go away, little rabbit!"

Lily did not go away. She jumped on the man's back and bit his ear. The man screamed and dropped his bag. The carrots fell out of the bag.

Lily grabbed as many carrots as she could and ran back to her burrow. She hid them under her bed. She was very happy. She had saved her carrots from the bad man.

The man got in his truck and drove away. He was very sad. He had no carrots for his soup. He had a sore ear and a bad day.

They danced together. They danced in circles, in lines, and in shapes. They danced with their arms, their legs, and their heads. They danced to the music, to the sound, and to the beat. They had fun. The people watched them. They clapped their hands. They liked to applaud.

He put the veil over his head and looked in the mirror. He smiled and said, "I am a bride! I am going to marry a prince!" He walked around the room, holding the veil like a train. He felt very happy and fancy.

But then, he heard his mom coming up the stairs. He knew she would be angry if she saw him with her veil. He tried to take it off, but it was stuck on his head. He pulled and tugged, but it would not come off. He started to panic and cry.

"Sam, what are you doing in my closet?" his mom asked, opening the door. She saw him with the veil and gasped. "Sam, that's my wedding veil! How did you get it?"

"I'm sorry, mom, I just wanted to play. I can't get it off, mom, it's stuck!" Sam sobbed.

His mom sighed and came over to him. She gently lifted the veil from his head and untangled it from his hair. She hugged him and said, "It's okay, Sam, I'm not mad at you. But you have to ask me before you touch my things, okay? And you have to be careful with them. This veil is very special to me. It was a gift from your dad when we got married."

"What is it, Sam?"

"Can I still be a bride when I grow up?"

His mom smiled and said, "Of course you can, Sam. You can be anything you want to be. But you don't need a veil to be a bride. You just need love."

Lily and Ben were best friends. They liked to play together in the park. One day, they saw a big sign that said: "Find the hidden prize and win a toy!" They wanted to win a toy, so they ran to the sign.

The sign had a map of the park. It showed where the prize was. It was under a big tree, near the pond. Lily and Ben followed the map. They looked for the big tree.

They found the big tree, but they did not see the prize. They looked under the leaves, under the rocks, under the branches. They did not find anything. They felt sad.

"Maybe someone else found the prize already," Lily said.

"Or maybe the prize is very small and we can't see it," Ben said.

They decided to look more carefully. They used their hands and their eyes to search. Then, Ben saw something shiny. It was a silver coin. He picked it up and showed it to Lily.

"Look, I found the prize!" he said.

Lily looked at the coin. It was very ordinary. It was not a toy. It was not fun. She did not think it was a prize.

"That's not a prize, that's just a coin," she said.

Ben felt confused. He thought the coin was a prize. He liked the coin. It was shiny and round and heavy. He wanted to keep it.

"But it was under the big tree, like the map said," he said.

Lily shrugged. She did not care about the coin. She wanted a toy. She looked at the map again. She saw something strange. The map had a big X on the other side of the pond. Maybe that was where the real prize was.

"Hey, Ben, look at this," she said. "Maybe the map was wrong. Maybe the prize is over there."

She pointed to the X. Ben looked at the coin and then at the X. He did not know what to do. He wanted to keep the coin, but he also wanted to see the prize.

He thought for a moment. Then, he smiled. He had an idea.

He gave the coin to Lily and said: "Here, you can have this. It's a prize for you. And I'll go with you to see the other prize. Maybe it's a prize for me."

Lily smiled too. She took the coin and put it in her pocket. She liked the coin now. It was a gift from Ben. And she wanted to see the other prize too. Maybe it was a toy.

They held hands and ran to the other side of the pond. They hoped to find the prize. They seemed happy. They were still best friends.

They decided to play with their toy kitchen. They pretended to make cakes and pies and cookies. They used flour and water and sugar and eggs. They made a big mess, but they had fun.

Then, they wanted to eat their pretend food. They looked for some cream to put on top. They found a can of whipped cream in the fridge. They took it to their toy kitchen and sprayed it on their plates.

"Yum, this looks good!" said Lily.

"Can I have some?" asked Ben.

"Sure, here you go," said Lily, and gave him some cream.

But Ben wanted more. He grabbed the can and sprayed more cream on his plate. And more. And more.

"Hey, stop it!" said Lily. "That's too much! You have to share!"

"No, I want it all!" said Ben. He demanded more cream. He did not listen to Lily. He did not care about sharing.

Lily was angry. She tried to take the can back from Ben. They started to fight. They pulled and pushed and shouted. They sprayed cream everywhere. On the floor, on the walls, on themselves.

Their mom heard the noise. She came to see what was going on. She saw the mess and the cream and the twins. She was not happy.

"What are you doing?" she asked. "Why are you wasting the cream? Why are you fighting?"

Lily and Ben stopped. They looked at their mom. They felt sorry. They knew they did something bad.

"We're sorry, mom," they said. "We were playing, but we got greedy. We wanted more cream. We did not share. We did not clean up."

"I'm gathering nuts to eat during the winter. I learned that it's important to prepare for the cold months," replied the squirrel.

Lily was amazed by the squirrel's bravery and wisdom. She decided to learn more from the animals in the woods and always be prepared for anything. From that day on, Lily spent more time in the woods, learning from the animals and becoming braver every day. And she never forgot the lesson she learned from the brave squirrel.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in the morning. One day, when she went outside, she saw her friend Jack. Jack was very enthusiastic about playing with Lily.

"Hi Jack! What do you want to play?" asked Lily.

"I want to play tag!" Jack replied.

"Okay, let's play!" said Lily.

As they were playing, Jack started to tease Lily. "You can't catch me!" he shouted while running away from her. Lily was getting a little upset, but then she saw a mist coming in. She thought it was magical and ran into the mist. When she came out, she surprised Jack by tagging him. They both laughed and continued playing together. The end.

Once upon a time, a little girl named Lily went to the river to play. She saw a crocodile swimming in the water. The crocodile had big teeth and a long tail. Lily thought the crocodile looked scary.

"Hello, little girl," said the crocodile. "What are you doing here?"

"I'm playing," replied Lily. "But you look scary with your big teeth and long tail."

The crocodile felt sad. "I'm sorry if I scared you," he said. "But I'm actually very friendly. And look, my favorite color is purple!"

Lily looked at the crocodile again and saw that he had a purple bow tied around his neck. She smiled and realized that sometimes things aren't always as they seem. From that day on, Lily and the crocodile became good friends and played together by the river. The moral of the story is to not judge someone based on their appearance, but to get to know them first.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in the sunshine. One day, she saw a red frog hopping in the grass. 

"Look, Mommy! A red frog!" Lily said. 

"Be careful, Lily. Frogs can be dangerous," Mommy warned. 

"I dare you to catch the frog!" Lily's friend, Timmy, said. 

Lily didn't want to be scared, so she tried to catch the frog. But when she got too close, the frog jumped and scared her. Lily fell down and hurt her knee. 

"Oh no! Are you okay, Lily?" Mommy asked. 

Lily cried and said, "I shouldn't have dared to catch the frog. It was too scary." 

From that day on, Lily learned to be careful and not take dares from her friends. And the red frog continued to hop in the grass, happy and free.

"Hello, Mr. Radio. Can we sing together?" asked Tweetie.

"Yes, we can!" replied the radio.

Tweetie and the radio sang together all day long. They sang so loud that all the animals in the garden came to listen. But as the sun went down, the radio suddenly stopped singing.

Ally asked her mommy if she could buy a yummy treat. Her mommy said yes, and Ally picked out a big, juicy piece of fruit. She loved how it tasted in her mouth!

On the way home, Ally noticed a tiny spot on one of her teeth. She looked and it and saw it had turned white! She was so happy that she held her mouth wide open and shouted "Mommy, look at my tooth!" 

Her mommy gave her a hug and said that now, it was time to take care of that tooth. She showed Ally how to brush and floss her tooth every day. Ally smiled and said that she loved her tooth even more now. 

They went home and Ally enjoyed her tasty treat even more. She smiled to herself, loving the feeling of happy, healthy teeth.

Once upon a time, there was a mighty dishwasher. It was so powerful that it could do all dishes in a few minutes. Every day, a mum and a dad used the dishwasher to do their dishes. 

One day, the dishwasher stopped working. The mum and dad could not understand why it was not working. So the dad called the repairman.

When the repairman came, he checked the dishwasher. After checking, he said that it needed a new part. The dad said he had no money. 

The repairman said that he did not need money. He wanted the dad to tell a lie. The dad was worried. He did not like to lie. But the repairman said it was the only way. He told the dad to lie to his boss and he will fix the dishwasher. 

So the dad told his boss a lie. Then he went back home. When he opened the door, he saw a surprise. The repairman had fixed the dishwasher. The mighty dishwasher was working again!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl. She liked to bathe in the big bathtub. It made her feel so warm and happy! She liked to splash around in the bath and play with her toys. 

One day while she was playing, she dropped her toy cell into the water. It sailed down to the bottom of the bath. The girl tried to catch it but it was too deep. She had to find another way to get it.

The girl grabbed a big spoon from the kitchen. She dipped it into the bath, swirling the water around. Suddenly, she spotted the toy cell at the bottom. She gently scooped it up and brought it to the surface.

The cell was covered with a thick layer of soap and bubbles. The girl giggled and set the cell aside. She then took the spoon and scooped the soapy water away. Underneath, the cell was all clean and sparkly again. 

The girl put the cell aside and slipped back into the bath. She felt so happy and snuggly. She couldn't wait for the next time she could bathe again.

But soon, the crab realised there was something he hadn't expected. A little boy was looking straight at him with a friendly smile and the sound he had heard wasn't a sneeze, it was a laugh! The little crab was so relieved that he waved his claws at the boy before scurrying away to find a safe place to hide.

The little crab was never that fearful again and always made sure to pay attention to the sounds around him.

Mary knocked on the door, and a kind yet stern voice answered. It was the voice of the igloo's owner, a polar bear! He invited her in, and when Mary stepped inside it was warm and cozy. 

The polar bear showed Mary around, and told her about the dangers of the chilly air outside. He showed her how to stay safe by putting on a special pair of shoes with tiny spikes on the soles.

After the tour, Mary decided to help the polar bear by washing up some dishes. With sudsy bubbles and a bit of elbow grease, the dishes were soon sparkling clean.

The polar bear thanked Mary and told her she could stay as long as she wanted, but Mary soon decided it was time to go. She waved goodbye, and after one final glance at the cozy igloo, Mary bravely returned to her own home.

"Why are you so smelly?" asked the witch.
The old banana answered "Because I rot!"

The witch was so astonished. She threw the banana away and went back to eating the yummy, fresh bananas. 

The witch learned her lesson and never asked a smelly banana a question again.

Sara said, "Oh, I am sorry. I did not know. Can I help you?"

The farmer said, "Sure, you can help me. You can ride with me on the tractor. We can take the wheat to the mill together."

Sara was happy. She said, "Thank you, farmer. That sounds fun."

She hugged her mom and dad and climbed on the tractor. The farmer drove the tractor to the mill. Sara saw how the wheat was turned into flour. She learned a lot. She had a peaceful day.

Ben wanted to feed the pigeon too, but he had no bread. He saw a shiny thing on the ground. It was a twist tie, like the ones that mom used to close the bread bag. Ben picked it up and twisted it into a shape. He thought it looked like a worm.

"Look, Lily, I have a worm!" Ben said, holding up the twist tie.

"No, Ben, that's not a worm, that's a twist tie. Pigeons don't eat twist ties, they eat bread," Lily said.

"But maybe this pigeon likes twist ties. Maybe it's a special pigeon," Ben said. He threw the twist tie to the pigeon.

The pigeon saw the twist tie and thought it was a worm too. It pecked at it and tried to eat it. But the twist tie was hard and sharp, and it hurt the pigeon's mouth. The pigeon spat out the twist tie and flew away.

"Ben, you scared the pigeon away! You made it sad!" Lily said, frowning at Ben.

"I'm sorry, Lily, I didn't mean to. I just wanted to feed the pigeon too," Ben said, feeling bad.

"Okay, mom," Ben and Lily said. They hugged mom back and said, "We love you, mom. You're great."

The boy looks at her and says, "No, I don't. Your guitar is silly. You can't play with my ball. Go away."

Anna feels sad. She does not like the boy. He is mean and bitter. She runs back to her mom and hugs her. She says, "Mom, the boy was rude to me. He did not want to play with me. He said my guitar is silly."

Her mom says, "I'm sorry, Anna. The boy was not nice. But you don't have to listen to him. Your guitar is beautiful. And you are a wonderful singer. You can play with anyone who is kind and friendly. Don't let him make you feel bad."

Anna smiles. She says, "Thank you, mom. You are right. I love my guitar. And I love you." She kisses her mom and plays her guitar again. She enjoys the sun and the birds. She hopes to find a new friend who likes music too.

Ben and Lily liked to play in the garden. They liked to dig holes, make mud pies, and chase bugs. One day, they saw a big ant hill near the fence. They wanted to catch some ants and look at them.

"Let's make a trap for the ants," Ben said. "We can use this cup and some bread crumbs."

"OK," Lily said. "But we have to be careful. Ants can bite."

They put the cup upside down on the ground, and made a small hole under it. Then they sprinkled some bread crumbs around the hole. They hid behind a bush and waited for the ants to come.

Soon, they saw a line of ants following the bread crumbs. Some of them went under the cup. Ben and Lily were very happy. They ran to the cup and lifted it up. They saw many ants inside, crawling and running.

"Wow, look at all the ants!" Ben said. "They are so small and fast."

"They have six legs and two feelers," Lily said. "And they are black and shiny."

They put the cup down again, and watched the ants. They wanted to see what the ants would do.

But the ants did not give up. They were very persistent. They worked together to make a new hole under the cup. They pushed and pulled and dug and bit. They made the hole bigger and bigger. Then they escaped from the trap.

Ben and Lily did not notice. They were busy talking and laughing. They did not see the ants running away. They did not see the hole under the cup.

After a while, they decided to check on the ants again. They lifted the cup and looked inside. They saw nothing. The cup was empty.

"Where are the ants?" Ben asked. "They are gone!"

"Maybe they flew away," Lily said. "Or maybe they dug a tunnel."

They looked around and saw the new hole under the cup. They saw the ants going back to their hill. They realized what had happened.

"The ants are very smart," Ben said. "They made their own trap for us."

"They tricked us," Lily said. "They are very clever."

They felt silly and amazed. They put the cup back on the ground and left some more bread crumbs for the ants. They said sorry to the ants and thanked them for the lesson. They learned that ants are not easy to catch. They learned that ants are very persistent and work together. They learned to respect the ants.

Sam and Mia were twins who liked to play in the park. One day, they saw a big puddle near the slide. Sam wanted to splash in the puddle, but Mia was nervous. She did not want to get wet and dirty.

"Come on, Mia, it's fun!" Sam said. He ran to the puddle and jumped in. He made a big splash and laughed. He splashed some more and got his shoes and pants wet.

"No, Sam, stop!" Mia said. She stayed away from the puddle. She wore her new leather shoes that Mom gave her. She did not want to ruin them. She liked her shoes. They were shiny and soft.

Sam did not listen to Mia. He kept splashing in the puddle. He did not see the man walking by with his dog. The man wore a nice suit and a hat. The dog wore a collar and a leash. Sam splashed the man and the dog by accident. The man and the dog got wet and angry.

"Hey, kid, what are you doing?" the man shouted. He was mad at Sam. He did not like to get wet and dirty. He did not like to see his suit and hat wet and dirty. He did not like to see his dog wet and dirty. He grabbed Sam by the arm and scolded him.

Mia saw what happened. She felt sorry for Sam. She ran to the man and said, "I'm sorry, sir, he did not mean to splash you. He was just playing. Please don't be mad at him."

The man looked at Mia. He saw her leather shoes. He saw that they were shiny and dry. He saw that she was polite and brave. He calmed down a bit. He let go of Sam and said, "Well, I guess you're right. He was just playing. But he should be more careful. He should not splash people and animals. He should respect their things. Do you understand, kid?"

Sam nodded. He felt ashamed. He said, "I'm sorry, sir, I was not careful. I did not respect your things. I will not splash people and animals again."

The man smiled. He said, "That's good, kid. I forgive you. But you should also apologize to your sister. She was worried about you. And you should take care of your shoes. They are nice shoes. They are leather shoes. Do you know what leather is?"

Sam shook his head. He did not know what leather was.

The man explained, "Leather is made from animal skin. It is strong and soft. But it can get damaged by water and dirt. You should keep your leather shoes clean and dry. They will last longer and look better."

Sam looked at his shoes. He saw that they were wet and dirty. He felt sad. He said, "I'm sorry, Mia, I did not take care of my shoes. They are leather shoes. They are nice shoes. You were right to be nervous. I was wrong to splash in the puddle."

Mia hugged Sam. She said, "It's okay, Sam, I forgive you. You can clean your shoes later. I'm glad you are okay. I love you, brother."

Sam hugged Mia back. He said, "I love you, sister. Thank you for helping me. You are brave and kind."

The man and the dog left. Sam and Mia went to the slide. They played together. They had fun. They learned a lesson. They learned to be careful, respectful, and grateful. They learned to love their leather shoes.

Lily was a smart girl who liked to learn new things. She had many books and toys in her room, but she wanted to see more of the world. One day, she saw a shiny rock in her neighbor's garden. She thought it was a mineral, and she wanted to look at it closely.

She asked her mom if she could borrow the rock for a while. Her mom said, "You have to ask your neighbor first. It is not nice to take things without permission. Maybe he will let you borrow it if you are polite and kind."

Lily nodded and went to the neighbor's door. She knocked and waited. The neighbor, Mr. Lee, opened the door and smiled. He was an old man who liked to collect rocks and fossils.

"Hello, Lily. What can I do for you?" he asked.

"Hello, Mr. Lee. I saw a shiny rock in your garden. It is very pretty. Can I borrow it for a while? I want to learn more about it. I will give it back to you soon, I promise," Lily said.

Mr. Lee was happy that Lily was interested in his hobby. He said, "Sure, you can borrow it. It is a quartz crystal. It is a kind of mineral that forms in the earth. It has many colors and shapes. You can use a magnifying glass to see its details. But be careful with it. It is fragile and can break easily."

"Thank you, Mr. Lee. I will be careful. You are very kind," Lily said. She took the quartz crystal and ran back to her room. She used a magnifying glass to see its sparkles and patterns. She learned a lot from the rock and had fun.

After a while, she remembered her promise. She wrapped the quartz crystal in a cloth and brought it back to Mr. Lee. She thanked him again and told him what she learned. Mr. Lee was proud of her and gave her a hug. He said, "You are welcome, Lily. You are a smart and honest girl. You can borrow more rocks from me anytime. I have many more to show you. Maybe you can be a geologist when you grow up."

Lily smiled and said, "Maybe I will. Thank you, Mr. Lee. You are a good friend."

The moral of the story is: It is good to be curious and learn new things, but it is also important to respect other people's belongings and keep your promises.

Mom looks at the man and says, "No, Tom, you can't. He is a stranger and we don't know him. He might not be nice or safe. You have to stay inside and play with your toy motorcycle."

Tom feels sad and curious. He says, "But mom, I just want to see his motorcycle. It is so big and loud. Maybe he will let me touch it or sit on it. Please, mom, please."

Mom shakes her head and says, "No, Tom, you can't. I'm sorry, but you have to listen to me. It is not polite to bother strangers or touch their things. Maybe someday you will have your own motorcycle, but for now, you have to be happy with your toy motorcycle."

Tom sighs and goes back to his room. He plays with his toy motorcycle, but he still looks at the window. He hopes the man with the motorcycle will come back another day. He wants to be his friend and learn more about motorcycles. He thinks motorcycles are the best thing in the world.

"Can I help?" asked Tommy.

"Yes, of course," smiled Mommy.

Tommy and Mommy worked together to build the campfire. They worked very hard and it took a long time. After they were done, Mommy started to light the campfire.

Suddenly, the campfire got very big and it made Tommy feel very dizzy. He started to cry and ran away. 

Mommy, worried, chased after Tommy. "It's OK Tommy," said Mommy. "I didn't mean to make you feel so dizzy."

Tommy looked up at Mommy and said, "It's OK Mommy. Just don't pour so much wood next time!" 

Mommy and Tommy hugged each other and started to laugh. Mommy promised Tommy that she would be more careful next time.

Once upon a time, there lived a green frog in a pond. Every morning, the frog would examine the pond for food. One morning, the frog met a fly. The frog didn't know that the fly was evil.

The frog asked the fly, "Why are you here?"
The fly replied, "I want to take your pond away from you."

The frog was so scared, but the fly seemed so friendly. So the frog allowed the fly to enter the pond.

But the fly was too greedy. He ate all the food the frog had collected for the day. Then the fly left, leaving the frog without any food.

The moral of this story is that you shouldn't trust a stranger. Even if they seem nice, danger can be lurking underneath.

One morning, Timmy went outside to play with his stick. But it was very cold outside. Timmy's hands were cold too. He held onto his stick tightly to keep his hands warm. Timmy was happy that he owned the stick because it helped him stay warm on a cold day.

One day, Lily went to the park with her mom. She brought her pink cushion with her and hung it on a tree branch while she played. But when it was time to go home, Lily forgot to take the cushion with her.

That night, Lily realized she had left her cushion at the park. She was sad and worried that someone might take it. The next day, Lily and her mom went back to the park to look for the cushion. But it was nowhere to be found.

Lily was heartbroken. She missed her cushion so much. She learned that it's important to always remember to take care of her things and not hang them up in places where they might get lost.

The big boy laughed. He did not care. He held the doll high above his head. He said, "This is a boring doll. It has no hair and no clothes. It is just skin and stuffing. I will throw it away."

He threw the doll as hard as he could. But he did not see the tree behind him. The doll hit the tree and bounced back. It hit the big boy in the face. He fell to the ground and dropped the doll. He cried and held his nose. It was bleeding.

Lily and Ben ran to the doll. They picked it up and hugged it. They were happy. They said, "Thank you, tree. You are our friend."

The big boy got up and ran away. He was scared and ashamed. He learned a lesson. He learned that being mean and greedy does not pay. He learned that he should yield to others and share. He learned that every doll has a story and a value, even if it is just skin and stuffing.

Tom and Mia were playing in the kitchen. They saw a big yellow fruit on the table. Tom said, "What is this? Can we eat it?" Mia said, "I don't know. Let's try it." They took the fruit and cut it in half. It smelled sour.

They each took a piece and put it in their mouths. They made a funny face and spit it out. It was very bitter and made their tongues hurt. They said, "Yuck! This is not good. This is a lemon. We don't like lemons." They threw the lemon pieces in the trash.

Then they heard a loud noise. It was their mom. She came into the kitchen and saw the mess. She was angry. She said, "Who did this? Who cut the lemon and wasted it? You know you are not allowed to use the knife. You could have hurt yourself. And you made a big mess. You are in trouble."

Tom and Mia were fearful. They did not want to get in trouble. They looked at each other and said, "Sorry, mom. We did not know. We wanted to try the lemon. We thought it was good. But it was not. It was bad. We don't like lemons. We won't do it again."

Mom looked at them and saw their funny faces. She remembered how she also tried a lemon when she was little and did not like it. She felt sorry for them. She said, "It's okay. I understand. You were curious. But you have to be careful. Lemons are not for eating. They are for making juice or dressing or cleaning. And you have to ask me before you use the knife. It is dangerous. Now, help me clean up the mess and then we can have some cookies."

Tom and Mia nodded and said, "Okay, mom. Thank you. We love you." They helped mom clean up the kitchen and then they had some cookies. They were sweet and yummy. They liked cookies. They laughed and hugged mom. They were happy.

Lily was not so happy. She felt cold and tired. She wanted to go home. She started to yawn.

Lily and Ben were very scared. They screamed and ran. But the cave was too big and dark. They did not know the way out. They got lost and trapped. The bear chased them and caught them. It was the end of Lily and Ben.

The moral of the story is: Do not go into places you do not know. Listen to your sister or brother. Be careful of what you wish for.

But they do not know that the shiny things are not toys. They are Mom and Dad's news. They are awards and medals and gifts. They are very important and special. They are for Mom and Dad's work. They help people and animals and plants.

Mom and Dad hear a loud noise. They run to the living room. They see Tim and Kim with the shiny things. They see the box is empty and torn. They are angry and sad. They shout at Tim and Kim. They say they are naughty and careless. They say they have to give back the shiny things. They say they have to say sorry.

Tim and Kim are scared and sorry. They cry and hug Mom and Dad. They say they are sorry. They say they did not know. They say they were curious. They say they wanted to test. They say they will not do it again.

Mom and Dad are still angry and sad. They say they love Tim and Kim. But they say they have to learn. They say they have to listen. They say they have to respect. They say they have to wait. They say they have to be careful.

They take the shiny things and put them back in the box. They say they have to fix them. They say they have to call some people. They say they have bad news. They say they have a lot of trouble. They say they have to go.

Tim and Kim are sad and sorry. They wish they did not open the box. They wish they did not play with the shiny things. They wish they did not make Mom and Dad angry and sad. They wish they did not have a bad ending.

Tim and Sam were brothers who liked to play in the yard. They had a big sack that they filled with leaves and sticks. They pretended it was a treasure and dragged it around. One day, they saw a small nail on the ground. It was shiny and sharp.

"Look, a nail!" Tim said. "Let's put it in our sack."

"OK," Sam said. "But be careful. It can hurt you."

They put the nail in their sack and kept playing. They did not know that the nail made a hole in the sack. Some of the leaves and sticks fell out. They did not see them.

They decided to hide their sack under a tree. They thought no one would find it there. They ran to the house to get some juice.

When they came back, they saw a big dog. It was sniffing their sack. It smelled the leaves and sticks. It wanted to play with them. It bit the sack and tore it open. The nail fell out. The dog saw the nail. It thought it was a bone. It picked it up with its mouth.

"Hey, that's our sack!" Tim shouted. "And our nail!"

They ran to the dog. They tried to get their sack and nail back. But the dog was bigger and stronger. It growled and barked. It did not want to share.

"Ow!" the dog yelped. It dropped the nail. It felt a pain in its mouth. The nail had poked its tongue. It was not a bone. It was a bad thing.

The dog ran away. It left the sack and the nail behind. Tim and Sam picked them up. They looked at the hole in the sack. They looked at the blood on the nail.

"Maybe we should not play with nails," Sam said.

"Maybe you are right," Tim said. "They are not fun. They are dangerous."

They threw the nail away. They emptied the sack. They did not want any more trouble. They went to find something else to play with. Something safe and nice.

One day, it was very gloomy outside. The sky was gray and it rained a lot. Anna could not go to the park or ride her bike. She was bored and sad. She decided to play with her toy phone. She pressed the button and waited for it to talk.

But the phone did not say anything. It was silent. Anna pressed the button again and again, but nothing happened. She shook the phone and hit it, but it still did not talk. She felt angry and frustrated. She threw the phone on the floor and started to cry.

Her mom heard her cry and came to see what was wrong. She saw the phone on the floor and picked it up. She opened the back and saw that the batteries were dead. She said, "Oh, Anna, I'm sorry. Your phone needs new batteries. That's why it doesn't talk. Do you want me to get some for you?"

Anna nodded and wiped her tears. She said, "Yes, please, mom. I want to play with my phone. I want to hear it talk and repeat." Her mom smiled and hugged her. She said, "Okay, sweetie. I'll be right back. Don't worry. Your phone will talk again soon." She went to get some new batteries for Anna's phone.

Anna felt better and waited for her mom. She hoped that her phone would work again and that the gloomy day would end soon. She wanted to hear her phone say something and then ask her to repeat. She thought that would make her happy.

One day, he was playing with his cars in his room, when he heard a loud roar outside. He ran to the window and saw a big truck with a shiny red motor. The truck was making a lot of noise and smoke. Leo was amazed. He wanted to see the truck up close.

He grabbed his favorite car, a blue one with a yellow stripe, and ran to the door. But the door was locked. His mom had locked it to keep him safe. Leo was frustrated. He banged on the door and shouted, "Mom, mom, let me out! I want to see the truck!"

His mom heard him and came to the door. She opened it and saw Leo's angry face. She smiled and said, "Leo, what's wrong? Why are you so upset?"

Leo pointed to the window and said, "The truck, the truck! I want to see the truck! It has a big motor and it roars!"

His mom looked outside and saw the truck. She understood why Leo was excited. She said, "I know, Leo, the truck is very cool. But you can't go outside by yourself. It's not safe. The truck is too big and loud. It might hurt you or scare you."

Leo frowned and said, "But I want to see the truck! Please, mom, please!"

His mom thought for a moment and said, "How about this, Leo? You can see the truck from the window, and I'll tell you more about it. Then, we can play with your cars together. Would you like that?"

Leo nodded and said, "Okay, mom, okay. But can I make the roar noise?"

His mom laughed and said, "Sure, Leo, you can make the roar noise. But not too loud, okay? We don't want to disturb the neighbors."

One day, a fox was walking in the forest. He saw a big hole in a tree. He thought it would be a good place to sleep. He went inside the hole and curled up.

But the hole was not cozy. It was full of sharp sticks and stones. The fox felt uncomfortable. He tried to move, but he hurt his paw. He cried out loud.

A bird heard the fox. She flew to the tree and looked inside the hole. She saw the fox and asked, "What is wrong, fox? Why are you crying?"

The fox said, "I wanted to sleep in this hole, but it is not nice. It is full of things that hurt me. And I cut my paw. It is bleeding."

The bird felt sorry for the fox. She said, "That is not a good hole, fox. It is broken. Someone needs to repair it. But I can help you. I have some soft feathers and leaves. I can make a bed for you. And I can wrap your paw with a leaf. It will stop the bleeding."

The fox smiled. He said, "Thank you, bird. You are very kind. Can you be my friend?"

The bird nodded. She said, "Yes, fox. I can be your friend. And I can show you a better hole to sleep in. It is not broken. It is cozy and warm."

The fox and the bird worked together. They made a bed for the fox in the hole. They wrapped his paw with a leaf. The fox felt better. He thanked the bird again.

Then the bird flew away. She said, "Follow me, fox. I will show you the way to the better hole."

The fox followed the bird. He was happy. He had a new friend and a new home. He hoped the better hole would not be uncomfortable.
