One day, a boy and a girl were playing in the garden. They liked to dig in the dirt and look for bugs and worms. They also liked to pretend they were explorers and find new things.

"Look, I found a big root!" the boy said, holding up a brown and twisted thing. "Maybe it is from a giant tree or a dinosaur!"

"Wow, that is cool!" the girl said. "Can I see it?"

The boy gave her the root and she felt it with her hands. It was hard and rough and had little hairs on it.

"Hey, this root is furry!" she said. "Maybe it is not a root at all, maybe it is a tail!"

"A tail?" the boy said. "What kind of tail?"

The girl thought for a moment. She remembered a book they had read about animals. She had an idea.

"Maybe it is a tail of a squirrel!" she said. "A squirrel that lives under the ground and hides its nuts there!"

The boy liked the idea. He imagined a furry squirrel with a big root for a tail. He smiled.

"That sounds fun!" he said. "Do you think we can find the squirrel?"

The girl nodded. She had a plan.

"I suggest we make a trap!" she said. "We can use this box and some string and some nuts. Then we can wait and see if the squirrel comes out!"

The boy agreed. They worked together to make a trap. They put some nuts inside the box and tied a string to it. They hid behind a bush and held the other end of the string.

They waited and waited. They hoped to see the furry squirrel with the big root tail. They wondered what it would look like and what it would do.

But no squirrel came out. Only a mole. A small and gray and blind mole. It sniffed the air and found the nuts. It crawled inside the box and started to eat.

The boy and the girl saw the mole. They were disappointed. They pulled the string and closed the box. They caught the mole.

They looked at each other. They did not know what to do with the mole. They felt sorry for it.

They decided to let it go. They opened the box and let the mole out. It scurried away and disappeared under the ground.

The boy and the girl looked at the root. They realized it was not a tail. It was just a root.

They laughed. They had made a silly mistake. They had a funny story to tell.

They put the root back in the dirt. They picked up their box and their string and their nuts. They went back to the house.

They had fun playing in the garden. They learned something new. They were happy.

Kitty jumped high in the air, did a flip, and landed on her feet. Tim clapped his hands and laughed. "Wow, Kitty! That was amazing!" Tim said. Kitty felt happy that she could make Tim smile.

Next, Kitty balanced a ball on her nose and walked on her back legs. Tim was so amazed that he forgot all about his lost toy. He applauded and laughed even more.

Kitty and Tim became best friends. They played together every day. Kitty's unique tricks and special value brought joy to everyone they met. And they all lived happily ever after.

Lily and Max played with the shiny balloon all day. They laughed and had a lot of fun. At the end of the day, Lily said, "Max, I'm glad we found our new friend, the shiny balloon. Even though it's not an angel, it's still special to us."

And from that day on, Lily and Max always remembered their special friend, the shiny balloon, and how it brought them joy. They learned that sometimes, the things we think we want can be different, but still make us happy.

"But I want it, Mommy," Timmy said. "It is so pretty and soft. Please, Mommy, please."

Mommy shook her head. "No, Timmy, I won't allow it. You have to respect the caterpillar and let it be. Maybe one day, it will turn into a butterfly and fly away. Then you can see how beautiful it is."

Timmy was not happy. He pouted and cried. He did not listen to Mommy. He waited until Mommy was busy and then he sneaked to the garden. He found the caterpillar on the same leaf. He reached out his hand and grabbed it.

"Ha, ha, I got you, caterpillar," he said. "Now you are mine."

But the caterpillar did not like to be held. It wriggled and tickled Timmy's hand. It also had tiny hairs that stung Timmy's skin. Timmy felt a sharp pain and dropped the caterpillar.

"Ow, ow, ow," he screamed. "The caterpillar hurt me. Mommy, Mommy, help me."

Mommy heard Timmy's cry and ran to the garden. She saw Timmy holding his hand and the caterpillar on the ground. She picked up the caterpillar and put it back on the leaf. She took Timmy inside and washed his hand. She put some cream and a bandage on it.

"Timmy, what did you do?" she asked.

"I took the caterpillar, Mommy," Timmy said. "I wanted to play with it. But it was bad. It bit me and made me hurt."

Mommy sighed. "Timmy, I told you not to take the caterpillar. You did not listen to me. You did not respect the caterpillar. You made a bad choice and you got hurt. Do you understand?"

Timmy nodded. He felt sorry and ashamed. He looked at his hand and saw the bandage. He looked at Mommy and saw her sad face.

"I'm sorry, Mommy," he said. "I'm sorry, caterpillar. I won't do it again. I will be good and listen to you. I will be kind and let the caterpillar be."

Mommy smiled and hugged Timmy. "That's good, Timmy. I'm glad you learned your lesson. I love you, Timmy. And I'm sure the caterpillar forgives you too."

The moral of the story is: Violence is wrong and hurts people. Music is beautiful and brings people joy. We should cherish our loved ones and our talents. We should not be greedy and cruel. We should be good and generous.

But sometimes, Anna and Ben get tired. They feel an urge to rest. They want to relax. They tell their mom and dad.

"Mom, dad, can we relax?" Anna asks.

"Sure, sweetie. Let's find a nice spot to sit down and have a snack," mom says.

They walk to a big tree. It has green leaves and brown bark. It gives them shade and cool air. They sit under the tree and eat some apples and crackers. They drink some water.

"Ah, this is nice. I feel better now," Ben says.

"Me too. I like to relax under the big tree," Anna says.

They climb on the tractor. They pretend to drive it. They make engine noises. Vroom, vroom. They are lively and excited. They do not see the farmer coming. He is angry. He shouts at them. "Hey, get off my tractor! You are not allowed to be here!"

Anna and Ben are scared. They jump off the tractor. They run to their moms. They say sorry to the farmer. The farmer is still angry, but he calms down. He says, "You should not play with things that are not yours. You could get hurt. The tractor is for work, not for play."

Anna and Ben nod. They understand. They feel bad. They say sorry again. They hug their moms. Their moms are not happy, but they forgive them. They say, "You should listen to us. We know what is best for you. We love you."

Anna and Ben say, "We love you too. We are sorry. We will not do it again." They hold their moms' hands. They leave the farm. They learn a lesson. They are still friends. They still like to play together. But they do not play with tractors anymore.

One day, her mom said, "Lily, it is time to eat. Come to the kitchen." Lily put down her book and went to the kitchen. She saw a plate of celery on the table. She did not like celery. She made a face.

"Mom, I do not want celery. I want cookies," she said.

"Sorry, Lily, but you have to eat some celery. It is good for you. It makes you strong and healthy. And you can have a cookie after you finish your celery," her mom said.

Lily did not believe her mom. She thought celery was yucky and bitter. She did not want to be strong and healthy. She wanted to be happy and sweet. She picked up a piece of celery and put it in her mouth. She chewed and chewed. She did not like it. She wanted to spit it out.

But then, she felt something crunchy and sweet in her mouth. She bit harder and tasted something yummy. She looked at the celery and saw a thin layer of peanut butter on it. She smiled.

"Mom, this celery is fine. It has peanut butter on it. I like peanut butter. Can I have more?" she asked.

Her mom smiled back. She had put peanut butter on the celery to make it more tasty for Lily. She was glad that Lily liked it. She gave her more celery and a cookie.

"Good girl, Lily. I am proud of you. You ate your celery and you liked it. Now you can read your book again. But first, give me a hug," her mom said.

Lily hugged her mom and thanked her. She took her book and her cookie and went back to her room. She was happy. She liked to read books and she liked to eat celery with peanut butter. She thought her mom was smart and kind. She read her book and ate her cookie. She had a good day.

Ben and Sam are friends. They like to play with cars. One day, they find a big car in the street. It is red and shiny. They want to drive it.

"Look, Ben, a car!" Sam says. "Let's go inside!"

"OK, Sam, but we need a license," Ben says. "A license is a paper that says you can drive."

"Where can we find a license?" Sam asks.

"Maybe in the car," Ben says. "Let's search!"

They open the door and climb in the car. They search in the glove box, in the seats, in the trunk. They do not find a license. They only find a lot of junk.

"Sam, this is not our car," Ben says. "This is someone else's car. We should not be here."

"But I want to drive," Sam says. "It looks fun."

"Sam, no!" Ben says. "It is not right to take what is not yours. And it is not safe to drive without a license. Come on, let's go."

But Sam does not listen. He turns the key and starts the car. He pushes the pedal and the car moves. He does not know how to steer or stop. He is scared.

"Help, Ben, help!" Sam cries.

Ben tries to help, but it is too late. The car hits a tree and makes a loud noise. The car is broken. Sam and Ben are hurt. They cry.

A man comes out of a house. He sees the car and the boys. He is angry. He is the owner of the car.

"Hey, what are you doing with my car?" he shouts. "You have no license! You have no right! You have made a big mess!"

He calls the police and the ambulance. They come and take Sam and Ben away. They are in trouble.

The moral of the story is: do not take what is not yours, and do not do what you are not allowed to do. You could hurt yourself and others, and get in trouble. Always listen to your friends who try to stop you from doing bad things.

She kissed the snowman on the cheek. "Bye, snowman. We will come back and play with you later."

She joined Mommy and Ben and went inside the house.

Sara and Ben were friends who liked to play with cars. They had many cars of different colors and sizes. They liked to race their cars on the floor and see who was faster.

One day, Sara had a new car that was very shiny and red. She said to Ben, "My car is the best. It has more speed than your car. Let us race and see who wins."

Ben agreed, but he was not happy. He liked his car, even if it was old and pale. He said, "My car may not have much speed, but it has more heart. Let us count to three and then start."

They counted, "One, two, three!" and pushed their cars on the floor. Sara's car zoomed ahead, but Ben's car followed close behind. Sara smiled and said, "I told you, my car is faster. I will win the race."

But then, something happened. Sara's car hit a bump and flipped over. It landed on its back and could not move. Ben's car passed by and reached the finish line. Ben stopped and said, "I won the race. My car may not have much speed, but it has more heart. It does not give up."

Sara felt sad and sorry. She said, "You are right, Ben. Your car has more heart. I was wrong to boast about my car. It does not matter how fast or shiny it is, if it cannot finish the race. I am sorry, Ben. Can we still be friends?"

Ben smiled and said, "Of course, Sara. We are still friends. And we can still play with our cars. But next time, let us not race, but share. Sharing is more fun than winning."

The moral of the story is: Do not be proud of what you have, but be grateful for what you have. And do not compete with others, but cooperate with them. Sharing is more fun than winning.

Anna and Ben are friends. They like to play together at school. One day, they have a new teacher. His name is Mr. Fox. He is fierce. He shouts at the children and makes them do hard work. He writes on the blackboard with a red pen. He says, "If you are bad, I will make you stand in the corner."

Anna and Ben are scared of Mr. Fox. They try to be good, but they make a mistake. They spill some water on the floor. Mr. Fox sees them and gets angry. He says, "You are bad children! You are messy and naughty! Go and stand in the corner now!"

Anna and Ben feel sad. They go and stand in the corner. They cry. They want their old teacher back. They miss her. She was kind and gentle. She smiled at the children and made them have fun. She wrote on the blackboard with a blue pen. She said, "If you are good, I will give you a sticker."

The other children see Anna and Ben crying. They feel sorry for them. They do not like Mr. Fox either. They think he is mean and scary. They want to help Anna and Ben. They have an idea. They whisper to each other and make a plan.

They wait until Mr. Fox is not looking. Then, they take his red pen and hide it. They find a blue pen and write on the blackboard. They write, "We are good children. We are friendly and happy. We like our old teacher. She is nice and sweet. Please bring her back."

Mr. Fox turns around and sees the blackboard. He is shocked and angry. He says, "Who did this? Who wrote on the blackboard? This is very bad! Tell me now or I will make you all stand in the corner!"

But the children do not tell him. They smile and say, "We do not know. We do not have a red pen. We only have a blue pen. We like blue. Blue is good."

Mr. Fox does not know what to do. He feels confused and silly. He realizes that the children do not like him. He realizes that he has been too fierce and harsh. He decides to change his ways. He says, "I am sorry, children. I have been wrong. I have been too fierce and harsh. I will try to be more kind and gentle. I will smile and make you have fun. I will write on the blackboard with a blue pen. I will say, 'If you are good, I will give you a sticker.'"

The children are happy. They clap and cheer. They forgive Mr. Fox. They give him a chance. They hope he will keep his promise. They hope he will be a good teacher. They hope their old teacher will come back soon.

The moral of the story is: Being fierce and harsh does not make people respect you. Being kind and gentle does.

The moral of the story is: Be kind to your friends and share your toys. Don't get mad or sad when accidents happen. Help each other and fix the problem.

They swing the net hard and hit the rose bush. The net gets stuck on the thorns and tears. The butterfly flies away and is free. Anna and Ben are sad and angry. They pull the net from the rose bush and see the holes.

"Oh no, we broke the net!" Anna says.

"Mom will be mad at us. She gave us the net for our birthday. It was new and nice." Ben says.

They look at each other and feel bad. They regret being so rough with the net. They wish they had been more careful. They know the net is fragile and can break easily.

They go to Mom and tell her what happened. They say they are sorry and ask for forgiveness. Mom is not happy, but she is not mad either. She hugs them and says she loves them. She says they can fix the net with some thread and a needle. She says they can still play with the net, but they have to be gentle and respectful with the things they catch.

Anna and Ben nod and say they understand. They thank Mom and help her fix the net. They learn their lesson and promise to be more kind. They still like to play with the net, but they also let the bugs and flowers go after they look at them. They do not chase the butterfly anymore. They watch it fly and smile.

Mom was not happy. She said, "Lily, you have to eat beef. It is good for you. It makes you strong and healthy. You cannot have cheese and bread and apples and milk every night. You have to try new things."

Lily shook her head. She said, "No, Mom. I do not like beef. It is yucky. It smells bad and tastes worse. I do not want to try it. I want cheese and bread and apples and milk."

Mom sighed. She said, "Lily, I know you are honest. You always tell me the truth. But sometimes, you have to be brave and polite. You have to eat what I make for you. You have to be thankful for what you have. You have to be a good girl."

Lily looked at her mom. She saw that her mom was sad and tired. She did not want to make her mom sad and tired. She wanted to make her mom happy and proud. She said, "Mom, I am sorry. I love you. I will try to eat beef. But can I have a little cheese and bread and apples and milk too?"

Mom smiled. She said, "Yes, Lily. You can have a little cheese and bread and apples and milk too. Thank you for being brave and polite and a good girl. I love you too." The bird didn't listen and kept trying to grab the sandwich. Timmy's mom came outside and saw what was happening. She shooed the bird away and gave Timmy a new sandwich, this time without any spicy stuff. Timmy was happy and ate his sandwich in peace. The end.

After a while, Timmy accidentally broke the scale. Lily was very upset and started to cry. Her mom tried to comfort her, but Lily was too sad. She learned that it's important to share, but it's also important to take care of your things.

Once upon a time, there was a crab. He lived in the sea and loved to play with his friends. One day, a bossy crab came along and told the crab that he had to sell his shell to him. The crab didn't want to sell his shell, but the bossy crab kept insisting.

Finally, the crab gave in and sold his shell to the bossy crab. But without his shell, the crab couldn't protect himself from predators. Sadly, he was eaten by a big fish.

The moral of the story is that you should never give in to someone who is bossy and wants you to do something you don't want to do. It's important to stand up for yourself and make your own decisions.

Once upon a time, there was a little birdie named Tweetie. Tweetie loved to fly high in the sky and feel the wind in his feathers. One day, Tweetie saw a big, tall mill in the distance. 

"Wow, that mill is so big!" Tweetie said to himself. 

As he flew closer, he noticed that the mill was not moving. "Why isn't the mill spinning?" he asked a friendly squirrel who was watching from below. 

"It's too cold," the squirrel replied. "The mill needs a warm breeze to spin." 

Tweetie decided to help. He flapped his wings as hard as he could and soared up into the sky. He flew higher and higher until he found a warm breeze. He flew back down to the mill and the warm breeze made the mill spin and spin. 

"Thank you, Tweetie!" the squirrel cheered. "You're a hero!" 

Tweetie felt proud and happy to have helped. He continued to soar through the sky, feeling the wind in his feathers.

Lily was happy that she could make a new friend just by being kind. From that day on, Lily always wore her pink dress to the park and looked for her new friend with a wink and a smile.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She was going on a trip with her family to the airport. Lily was very excited to go on an airplane for the first time, but also a little frightened. 

As they arrived at the airport, Lily saw lots of big planes taking off and landing. She held her mommy's hand tightly and said, "Mommy, I'm scared." 

Her mommy hugged her and said, "Don't worry, sweetie. I promise you'll be safe with us." Lily felt better and they went to check in for their flight. 

While waiting at the gate, Lily overheard a little boy talking to his dad. "I'm so excited to see my grandma!" he said. Lily smiled and said to him, "I'm going on an airplane too!" They became friends and played together until it was time to board the plane. 

Lily held her daddy's hand as they walked down the aisle to their seats. She looked out the window and saw the clouds passing by. "This is so cool!" she said. Her family smiled and they all enjoyed the flight together.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside with her friends. One day, they decided to play hide-and-seek in the dark. Lily was scared of the dark, but she wanted to play with her friends, so she brought her flashlight.

As they were playing, Lily's friend, Timmy, found her and said, "I found you! You're it now, Lily!" Lily didn't want to be it, so she shrugged and said, "I don't want to be it, Timmy. Can we play something else?" 

Timmy looked at Lily's flashlight and said, "That's an ugly flashlight, Lily." Lily felt sad, but she didn't want to argue, so she just shrugged again and said, "It's my favorite flashlight, Timmy." 

They decided to play tag instead, and Lily had so much fun running around with her friends. She didn't even need her flashlight anymore. From that day on, Lily realized that it didn't matter what her friends thought of her flashlight. As long as she loved it, that's all that mattered.

Once upon a time, there was an old lady. She was very old and her hair was white like snow. She lived in a house with a big white box called a freezer. The freezer kept her food cold so it wouldn't go bad.

One day, the old lady forgot to put her ice cream in the freezer. She left it out on the counter and it melted. She was sad because she loved ice cream. Her granddaughter came to visit and reminded her to put her ice cream in the freezer so it wouldn't melt again.

The old lady was very happy that her granddaughter reminded her. She gave her a big hug and said thank you. From that day on, the old lady always put her ice cream in the freezer. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a big hippo. His name was Harry. Harry was very hungry and he wanted to eat all the grass in the field. Harry ate and ate until he was full. Then, Harry felt happy because he finished eating all the grass. 

But one day, Harry felt anxious. He was scared because he heard a loud noise. Harry looked around and saw a lion. The lion was very big and Harry was scared. Harry ran away as fast as he could. 

Finally, Harry reached a river. He saw his reflection in the water and realized he was safe. Harry was happy because he finished running away from the lion.

There was a little duck named Ducky who lived by a big swamp. Ducky was nervous because he had to write a letter to his friend, but he didn't know how to write. He waddled around the swamp looking for someone to help him.

Suddenly, he saw a wise old owl sitting on a tree branch. Ducky asked the owl for help with his letter. The owl said, "Sure, I can help you! What do you want to write about?"

Ducky told the owl about his adventures in the swamp and how much he missed his friend. The owl helped Ducky write the letter and Ducky was very happy. He thanked the owl and happily waddled back to his home by the swamp.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy had a teddy bear that he loved to hug every night before bed. One day, Timmy went to the park to play with his friends. He brought his teddy bear with him, but he accidentally dropped it and didn't notice.

When it was time to go home, Timmy realized his teddy bear was missing. He looked everywhere but he couldn't find it. Timmy was sad and started to cry. His friends saw him crying and asked what was wrong. Timmy told them he lost his teddy bear.

Timmy's friends wanted to help him, so they all started looking for the teddy bear. One of his friends found it in a tree. It was stuck up high and they couldn't reach it. Timmy's brilliant idea was to attach a stick to a rope and use it to pull the teddy bear down. They tried it and it worked! Timmy was so happy, he hugged his teddy bear tightly and thanked his friends for helping him find it.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. One day, Lily was walking in the forest when she saw a big, scary bear. The bear was very angry and growling loudly. Lily was scared and didn't know what to do.

Suddenly, she remembered something her mommy had told her. "When you're in trouble, don't fight. Surrender and be calm." So, Lily closed her eyes, took a deep breath, and surrendered to the bear. The bear sniffed her and then walked away.

Lily learned that sometimes it's better to surrender than to fight. She also learned that the dark forest can be scary, but if you stay calm, you can overcome your fears. From that day on, she was never afraid of the dull darkness in the forest again.

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Lily who had a big, red ball. She loved to play with it every day. One day, Lily's friend Timmy came over to play. Timmy asked Lily if he could play with her ball, but Lily said no because it was special to her.

Timmy got sad and said, "I wish I had a ball like that."

Lily thought for a moment and said, "I have an idea! Let's trade. You can have my ball and I can have your toy car."

Timmy was happy with the idea and they made the trade. But after a few days, Lily realized that the toy car was not as fun as she thought it would be. She missed her ball.

So, Lily went to Timmy and asked, "Can we reverse the trade? I want my ball back."

Timmy said, "Sure, but I want something in return."

Lily asked, "What do you want?"

Timmy replied, "I want to marry your doll."

Lily thought it was a cheap price to pay to get her ball back, so she agreed. They reversed the trade and Lily was happy to have her ball back. Timmy was happy too because he got to marry Lily's doll.

Tom and Mia like to play with blocks. They build towers and houses and bridges. They have many colors of blocks: red, blue, yellow, green. They have fun making different things.

One day, they want to make a very high tower. They use all the blocks they have. They put one block on top of another, and another, and another. The tower is huge. It is taller than Tom and Mia. It is taller than the table. It is taller than the chair.

Tom and Mia are happy. They want to show their tower to Mom and Dad. They run to the door and sign to them. Sign means to use their hands to talk. Tom and Mia cannot hear with their ears, but they can see with their eyes. They sign "Come, come, see our tower!"

Mom and Dad come and see the tower. They are proud of Tom and Mia. They sign "Wow, wow, what a huge tower! You are very clever!" They hug and kiss Tom and Mia.

But then, something happens. The wind blows through the window. It makes the tower shake. The blocks start to fall. One by one, they crash to the floor. The tower is gone.

Tom and Mia are sad. They sign "Oh, oh, our tower is broken!" They cry and cry.

Mom and Dad hug and kiss them again. They sign "It's okay, it's okay. You can make another tower. You still have all the blocks. You can try again. We love you!"

Tom and Mia stop crying. They smile and nod. They sign "Yes, yes, we can make another tower. We love you too!" They pick up the blocks and start to build again. They are happy.

Tom and Lily were playing with a ball in the park. They liked to pass the ball to each other and catch it. Sometimes they missed and the ball rolled away.

One day, a big man came and took their ball. He said it was his ball and they could not have it. Tom and Lily were sad and angry. They asked for their ball back, but the big man said no and walked away.

Tom and Lily ran after the big man. They wanted their ball. They shouted and cried. The big man did not stop. He crossed the street with their ball.

A police car was driving fast on the street. It had a loud noise and a bright light. The police car did not see the big man. The big man did not see the police car. The police car hit the big man and the ball.

Tom and Lily stopped and watched. They were scared and shocked. The big man fell down and did not move. The ball popped and flew away. The police car stopped and the police came out. They looked at the big man and the ball. They looked different. They looked broken.

Tom and Lily did not play with the ball anymore. They went home and hugged their mom and dad. They did not like the park anymore. They did not like the big man anymore. They did not like the police car anymore. They did not like the ball anymore.

Lila and Tom were playing in the park. They liked to run and slide and swing. They saw a big sack on the grass. It was brown and dirty and had holes in it.

"Look, a sack!" Lila said. "What is inside?"

"I don't know. Let's see!" Tom said. They ran to the sack and opened it. Inside, they saw many pigeons. The pigeons were gray and white and had red feet. They were scared and noisy.

"Wow, pigeons!" Lila said. "They are so pretty!"

"Shh, don't scare them!" Tom said. "Maybe they are lost. We should help them."

They tried to pick up the pigeons, but the pigeons did not like it. They flapped their wings and pecked their hands. They flew out of the sack and into the sky.

"Ouch, ouch, ouch!" Lila and Tom said. "The pigeons are powerful! They hurt us!"

They ran away from the sack and the pigeons. They saw a man coming to the park. He had a hat and a coat and a net. He looked angry.

"Hey, you kids!" the man shouted. "What did you do to my sack? Those are my pigeons! I catch them for money!"

Lila and Tom were scared of the man. They did not know he was bad. They thought he was the owner of the pigeons.

"We are sorry, mister!" Lila said. "We did not know they were yours. We wanted to help them."

"Help them? You let them go!" the man said. "They are worth a lot of money! You owe me!"

He ran after Lila and Tom with his net. He wanted to catch them and make them pay. But Lila and Tom were faster. They ran to their mom and dad, who were sitting on a bench. They told them what happened.

"Mom, dad, help us!" Lila and Tom said. "There is a bad man who wants to catch us! He has a sack and a net and pigeons!"

Mom and dad looked at the man. They saw he was mean and greedy. They did not like him. They stood up and faced him.

"Leave our kids alone!" mom said. "They did nothing wrong. You are the one who is wrong. You should not catch pigeons. They are free and beautiful. They belong to the sky, not to your sack!"

"Yeah, what she said!" dad said. "And if you don't go away, we will call the police. They will take you and your sack and your net and put you in jail!"

The man was afraid of mom and dad. He was afraid of the police. He did not want to go to jail. He dropped his sack and his net and ran away. He did not come back.

Lila and Tom hugged mom and dad. They were happy and safe. They thanked them for saving them.

"Thank you, mom and dad!" Lila and Tom said. "You are powerful! You scared the bad man away!"

Mom and dad smiled and kissed them. They were proud of them.

"You are welcome, Lila and Tom!" mom and dad said. "You are brave and kind! You helped the pigeons!"

They looked at the sky. They saw the pigeons flying and singing. They were free and happy. They thanked Lila and Tom too.

"Thank you, Lila and Tom!" the pigeons said. "You are our friends!"

The end.

One day, they have a big fight over a charming doll. Anna says, "The doll is mine! I saw it first!" Ben says, "No, the doll is mine! I like it more!" They pull the doll and make it cry.

Mom hears the doll cry and comes to see. She is not happy. She says, "Anna and Ben, you are twins. You should love each other and share. Fighting is not nice. It makes the doll sad and it makes me sad. How can you improve your behavior?"

Anna and Ben feel sorry. They do not want to make the doll or mom sad. They say, "We are sorry, mom. We will improve our behavior. We will love each other and share." They hug mom and the doll.

Mom smiles and says, "That's good, Anna and Ben. I am proud of you. You are charming twins. Now you can play nicely with the doll and your other toys." Anna and Ben nod and say, "Thank you, mom." They play nicely with the doll and their other toys. They are happy.

Mom was not happy. She said, "Ben, novels are good, but you need to speak too. Speaking is important. You need to express yourself and listen to others. You need to make friends and share your feelings. You can't just read novels all the time."

Ben was not happy. He said, "Mom, you don't understand. Novels are my friends. They make me happy and smart. I don't like to speak. Speaking is hard and boring. I don't care about other people's feelings. I just want to read novels."

Lily loved to whistle. She whistled all the time, when she played, when she ate, when she brushed her teeth. She whistled so much that her mom and dad sometimes asked her to be quiet. But Lily did not mind. She liked to make music with her mouth.

One day, Lily was whistling in her room, when she heard a knock on the window. She looked and saw a big white bird with shiny wings. It was an angel! Lily was surprised and happy. She opened the window and said hello.

"Hello, little girl," the angel said. "I heard your whistling and I came to see you. You have a beautiful voice."

"Thank you, angel," Lily said. "Do you like to whistle too?"

"Yes, I do," the angel said. "Whistling is a way to praise God and to share joy. Would you like to whistle with me?"

Lily nodded. She was very excited. She and the angel whistled together, making incredible sounds. They whistled high and low, fast and slow, loud and soft. They whistled songs and tunes and melodies. They whistled until the sun set and the stars came out.

Lily felt very happy. She had never whistled with anyone before. She thanked the angel for coming and asked if he would come again.

"Of course, I will," the angel said. "You are my whistling friend. I will come whenever you whistle for me. Just remember to be kind and grateful and to love God and your family."

Lily smiled and hugged the angel. She said goodbye and closed the window. She went to bed and dreamed of whistling with the angel again. She felt very blessed. She was a whistling girl with an angel friend.

Anna was curious. She wanted to see how the needle worked. She asked her mom, "Can you show me how to sew, mom?"

"Who lives in the bad house?" Lily asks.

"Maybe a monster," Tom says.

They are scared. They want to go away. But then they hear a sound. It is a small sound, like a cry.

"Hello?" Lily says. "Is someone there?"

They go closer to the bad house. They see a hole in the wall. Inside the hole, there is a cat. The cat is hurt. It has a cut on its leg. It is hungry and cold.

"Look, Tom, a cat!" Lily says.

The cat looks at them. It is afraid. It does not know them.

"Don't be scared, cat," Tom says. "We are friends. We care about you."

Lily and Tom are kind. They take the cat out of the hole. They wrap it in a scarf. They give it some bread and water. They pet it gently.

The cat feels better. It purrs. It likes Lily and Tom.

"Can we keep the cat?" Lily asks.

"Sure," Tom says. "We can take it to our house. Our house is good. It has a door, a window, a roof. It is clean and bright. We have a bed for the cat. We have food and toys for the cat. We have love for the cat."

Lily and Tom are happy. They have a new friend. The cat is happy. It has a new home. They leave the bad house. They go to the good house. They are a family.

Anna was a tall girl who liked to cut paper with scissors. She made many shapes and animals with her paper. She was very good at cutting and gluing.

One day, she had an exam at school. The teacher gave her a paper with some lines and dots. She had to cut along the lines and make a circle, a square and a triangle. Anna was happy. She knew how to cut well.

She took her scissors and started to cut. But she cut too fast and too hard. She cut the paper and her finger. She felt a sharp pain and saw some red on her finger. She cried out loud.

"Ow, ow, ow! I cut myself! It hurts!"

The teacher heard her and came to see. She saw Anna's finger and the paper. She took a tissue and wrapped it around Anna's finger. She said:

"Oh, Anna, I'm sorry. You cut yourself. Don't worry, it's not a big cut. It will stop bleeding soon. Let me see your paper. You did a good job. You cut the shapes very well. You are a smart girl."

Anna felt a little better. She looked at her paper and smiled. She was proud of her shapes. She said:

"Thank you, teacher. I like to cut paper. But I will be more careful next time. I don't want to cut myself again."

The teacher nodded and smiled. She said:

"You're welcome, Anna. I like your paper too. But yes, you have to be careful with scissors. They are sharp and can hurt you. Next time, cut slowly and gently. And if you need help, ask me or a friend. OK?"

Anna nodded and said:

"OK, teacher. I will do that. Can I have a band-aid for my finger?"

The teacher said:

"Of course, Anna. Here you go. A band-aid with a star. You are a star, Anna. A tall and smart star who can cut paper very well."

Anna put the band-aid on her finger and thanked the teacher. She felt happy and proud. She finished her exam and showed her paper to her friends. They liked her shapes and said she was a good cutter. Anna smiled and said:

"Thank you, friends. You are good cutters too. But be careful with scissors. They can cut you too."

Spike was a dog. He was old and big. He had black fur and a long tail. He liked to sleep and eat. He did not like to play or run.

One day, a girl came to Spike's house. She was small and cute. She had red hair and a pink dress. She wanted to play with Spike. She asked him, "Can I play with you, Spike?"

Spike opened one eye and looked at her. He did not want to play. He wanted to sleep. He said, "No, go away. I am old and tired."

The girl was sad. She liked Spike. She wanted to be his friend. She asked him again, "Please, Spike, can I play with you? I have a ball and a bone. We can have fun."

Spike closed his eye and growled. He did not want to have fun. He wanted to eat. He said, "No, leave me alone. I am old and hungry."

The girl was very sad. She started to cry. She did not understand why Spike was so mean. She asked him one more time, "Why, Spike, why are you so mean? I just want to play with you. Don't you like me?"

Spike heard her cry. He felt sorry for her. He opened both eyes and looked at her. He saw that she was nice and sweet. He said, "I'm sorry, little girl. I am not mean. I am just old and grumpy. I do like you. You can play with me."

The girl stopped crying and smiled. She was happy. She said, "Thank you, Spike. You are a good dog. I like you too. You can play with me."

Spike got up and wagged his tail. He was happy too. He said, "You're welcome, little girl. You are a good girl. I can play with you."

They played with the ball and the bone. They had fun. They became friends. Spike was not old and grumpy anymore. He was old and happy.

"Let's play hide and seek!" Lily said. "You count to ten and I'll hide in the leaves."

"Okay," Tim said. He closed his eyes and started to count. "One, two, three..."

Lily ran to the pile of leaves and dove in. She covered herself with the leaves and waited for Tim to find her. She thought it was a good hiding spot.

"Ten!" Tim shouted. He opened his eyes and looked around. He saw the rake leaning against the fence. He thought it was boring. He wanted to find Lily. He walked to the pile of leaves and kicked it with his foot.

"Ow!" Lily cried. She popped out of the leaves and rubbed her head. "That hurt!"

"Sorry, Lily," Tim said. "I didn't know you were there. I thought you were hiding somewhere else."

"That's not fair," Lily said. "You cheated. You're supposed to look for me, not kick me."

"I'm sorry, Lily," Tim said again. "I was just trying to have fun. Do you want to play something else?"

Lily looked at Tim and saw that he was sorry. She forgave him and smiled. "Okay, Tim. Let's play something else. But no more kicking, okay?"

"Okay, Lily," Tim said. "No more kicking. How about we spring on the trampoline?"

"Yay!" Lily said. "I love the trampoline. Let's go!"

But then, Mia made a face. She spat out her ice cream and said, "Ew, Mia, this is bitter!"

Ben looked at her ice cream and saw something brown and slimy on it. It was the worm! It had stuck to Mia's hand and got on her ice cream. Ben screamed and dropped his ice cream too. He ran away from the worm and said, "Yuck, Mia, that's gross!"

Mia was mad and sad. She threw her ice cream at the worm and said, "Bad worm, bad worm, you ruined my ice cream!"

The worm didn't care. It crawled away and looked for a new home. Mia and Ben learned a lesson: always wash your hands after playing with worms.

One day, a white duck was walking to the pond with her friends. She saw a farmer working in his field. He had a big hat and a shovel. The duck was curious and wanted to talk to him.

"Hello, farmer!" the duck said. "What are you doing?"

The farmer looked up and smiled. "Hello, duck. I am digging holes for my seeds. I want to grow corn and carrots and beans."

"That sounds fun," the duck said. "Can I help you?"

The farmer shook his head. "No, thank you, duck. You have to go to the pond with your friends. It is time for your swim and your lunch."

The duck nodded, but she did not want to leave. She liked the farmer and his field. She decided to delay her swim and her lunch. She stayed with the farmer and watched him dig. She asked him many questions and he answered them kindly.

Meanwhile, her friends waited for her at the pond. They were hungry and bored. They wondered where the duck was. They called her name, but she did not hear them. They started to worry. They thought she might be lost or in trouble.

Then, the dog sprayed something black all over Timmy's face. Timmy was confused and scared, but then he realized it was just black paint from the dog's tail. Timmy laughed and hugged the dog. He was happy that he got his truck back and made a new friend.

Once upon a time, there was a little rabbit named Benny. He loved to eat carrots. One day, Benny went to the garden to look for some carrots. He heard a loud noise and got scared. 

Suddenly, a big dog appeared. "Hey little rabbit, what are you doing here?" asked the dog. "I am looking for some carrots," replied Benny. 

The dog was very obedient and said, "I will help you find some carrots." They searched together and finally found some delicious carrots. Benny was very happy and thanked the dog. "I am glad I heard you and came to help," said the dog. From that day on, they became good friends and looked for carrots together every day.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to eat soup, especially tomato soup. One day, Lily's mommy made her soup for lunch. But when Lily took a bite, she noticed that the soup was not clear. It was very cloudy and she couldn't see through it. 

Lily didn't like her soup like this. She wanted it to be clear. So, she decided to solve the problem. She asked her mommy if she could strain the soup through a sieve. Her mommy said yes and helped her do it. 

After they strained the soup, it became clear and Lily was very happy. She ate her soup and it tasted delicious. From that day on, whenever Lily's soup was cloudy, she knew how to solve the problem and make it clear again.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in the sun. One day, Lily decided to go for a walk in the woods. She saw a big mill and went inside to explore. 

Inside the mill, Lily met a thin old man who was working. "Hello there, what are you doing?" asked Lily. "I am grinding wheat into flour," replied the old man. "Would you like to help me?" 

Lily was excited to help and started to turn the handle. But then, the mill suddenly stopped working. "Oh no, the mill is broken," said the old man. "We need to dry the gears before we can fix it." 

Lily didn't know how to dry the gears, so she went outside to look for help. She saw a group of boys playing nearby and asked for their help. But the boys didn't want to help and laughed at her instead. 

Lily felt sad and went back to the mill. The old man was still trying to fix the mill, but it was too late. The gears were too damaged and the mill was ruined. "I'm sorry, Lily. We can't fix the mill now," said the old man. 

Lily felt even sadder and wished she could have fixed the mill. She learned that sometimes bad things happen and it's important to ask for help.

Tim thought for a moment and said, "Let's sit under the tree together. The big bird won't see us there." So, Tim and the frog sat under the tree, feeling safe and happy. They became good friends and played near the hill every day.

Ruby was sad because her friends could not play. She had an idea. She told her friends to come to her warm tree house. They all went to the tree house and were happy. They played inside the warm tree house until the cold went away. When the ice melted, they went outside to play in nature again.

One day, Lila went to the forest with her family. They wanted to have a picnic and play. Lila loved the forest. She saw many trees, leaves, and mushrooms. She smelled the fresh air and the flowers. She touched the bark, the grass, and the rocks.

Just then, Timmy's little sister found a lantern in the bottom of their camping bag. Timmy was so happy and relieved! He hugged his sister and thanked her for finding the lantern. They all went to sleep feeling safe and happy. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in the sun with her friends. One day, she saw a big mill on the hill. She asked her mom, "What's that big thing on the hill?" Her mom answered, "That's a mill, sweetie. It makes flour for bread."

Lily was curious and wanted to know more. She asked her mom, "How does the mill make flour?" Her mom patiently answered, "The mill has big stones inside that grind the wheat into flour." Lily was amazed and wanted to see it for herself.

So, Lily went to the mill and asked the miller, "Can I see how the mill works?" The miller answered, "Of course, I'll show you." Lily watched as the miller poured the wheat into the mill and the stones started to turn. She was happy to have her question answered and thanked the miller for showing her how the mill works.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play with his toys and go on adventures. One day, Timmy went on a walk with his mommy and they saw a big colorful factory. Timmy was so excited! He wanted to go inside and see what was there.

As they walked closer to the factory, they met a man who worked there. The man was very nice and he asked Timmy if he wanted to see inside the factory. Timmy was so happy! They went inside and saw all the machines making things. Timmy saw lots of colorful things being made, like toys and candy.

After they left the factory, Timmy told his mommy that he wanted to work in a colorful factory when he grew up. His mommy smiled and said that was a great idea. Timmy was so happy that he got to meet someone who worked in a factory and see all the colorful things being made.

Once upon a time, there was a parrot named Polly. Polly was a very smart and independent bird. She loved to fly around and eat seeds.

One day, Polly saw a banana that she really wanted to eat. But the banana was up high on a shelf. Polly didn't know what to do. Then, she saw her friend, a monkey, pass by. 

Polly asked the monkey for help. The monkey was happy to help and passed the banana down to Polly. Polly was so happy and thanked the monkey. From that day on, Polly and the monkey were good friends and passed things to each other all the time.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside with her friends. One day, Lily and her friends were playing with a ball when her mom called her to come inside. 

"Come inside, Lily. It's time to eat," said her mom.

Lily was sad to leave her friends, but she went inside. When she sat down to eat, her mom gave her some vegetables and said, "Eat your vegetables so you can grow big and strong."

Lily didn't like vegetables, but she ate them anyway. After dinner, her mom took out a scale and asked Lily to stand on it. She recorded her weight and said, "You're growing so fast! Eating healthy food keeps you safe and strong."

From that day on, Lily ate her vegetables every day. She knew that being healthy was important and she wanted to be strong like her mom.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She was very hungry and wanted something to eat. She went to her mommy and said, "Mommy, I am so hungry. Can we have some food?" Her mommy said, "Yes, let's go to the kitchen and discuss what we can eat."

While they were in the kitchen, Lily saw her notebook on the table. She said, "Mommy, can I draw in my notebook while we discuss what to eat?" Her mommy said, "Yes, of course you can."

Lily drew a picture of a big sandwich while they discussed what to eat. Finally, they decided to make peanut butter and jelly sandwiches. Lily was so happy and no longer hungry. She ate her sandwich while looking at her notebook and feeling very proud of her drawing.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her toys on the table. One day, she accidentally knocked over a cup of juice on the table and it made a big mess. Her mom got angry and told her to be careful next time.

Later that day, Lily was playing with her toys again when she heard a loud noise. She looked up and saw a big scary dog outside her window. The dog started barking and it scared her. She quickly climbed onto the table to get away from the dog. 

Lily's mom heard the commotion and came to see what was wrong. When she saw the dog, she called the animal control and they came to take the dog away. Lily was very happy that she was safe and she promised to always be careful when playing on the table.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a big teddy bear named Brownie. One day, Lily went to play outside with Brownie. She saw a flower and picked it up. It was very pretty! 

Lily hugged Brownie and said, "Look, Brownie! I picked a flower!" Brownie smiled and hugged her back. 

After a while, Lily got thirsty and went inside to get some water. She saw an empty glass on the table. "Oh no!" she said. "The glass is empty. I need to fill it with water." 

Lily's mom heard her and said, "I will fill the glass for you, Lily." Lily smiled and hugged her mom. "Thank you, Mommy!" she said.

Lily was very happy. Today was her birthday. She had a new dress and a new cake. She invited her friends to her part. They played games and sang songs.

Then, a clown came to the part. He had a big red nose and funny clothes. He made jokes and tricks. He made balloons into animals and hats. Lily and her friends laughed and clapped.

"Hello, little girl," the clown said to Lily. "What is your name?"

"I am Lily," she said. "It is my birthday."

"Happy birthday, Lily!" the clown said. "Do you like your new dress?"

"Yes, I do," Lily said. "It is pink and pretty."

The clown smiled. "You are very sweet, Lily. Do you want a special balloon?"

"Yes, please," Lily said.

The clown blew a balloon and twisted it. He made a flower for Lily. He gave it to her and said, "This is for you, Lily. A new flower for a new dress. I hope you have a wonderful part."

Lily hugged the clown and said, "Thank you, clown. You are very nice. I love my flower and my part."

The end.

Lily and Tom were on a trip with their mom and dad. They drove a long time in the car until they came to a big forest. There was a cabin in the forest where they could sleep. Lily and Tom liked the cabin. It was cozy and had a fireplace and a lot of books.

One night, Lily and Tom heard a strange noise outside the cabin. It sounded like a howl. They were scared and ran to their mom and dad's room.

"Mom, dad, what is that noise?" Lily asked.

"It's a wolf, honey. Don't worry, it won't come near the cabin. It's just looking for food in the forest," dad said.

"Why does it howl like that?" Tom questioned.

"It's how wolves talk to each other. They howl to say hello, or to warn, or to find their mates. They are very smart animals, but they are also shy and like to be quiet," mom said.

"Can we see the wolf?" Lily asked.

"Maybe in the morning, if we are lucky. But we have to be very quiet and careful, and not scare the wolf away. Wolves are wild and don't like people very much," dad said.

Lily and Tom nodded. They were curious about the wolf, but they also respected it. They snuggled with their mom and dad and fell asleep. The cabin was quiet, except for the occasional howl of the wolf in the forest.

Ben and Lily were walking on the path with their mom. They liked the path because it had many flowers and birds and bugs. But today the path was boring. There was nothing new to see or hear or smell.

"Mom, can we go back home?" Ben asked. He was tired and hungry.

"Not yet, sweetie. We have to go to the store and buy some milk and eggs," Mom said. She smiled at Ben and Lily. "But I have a surprise for you when we get there."

"What is it?" Lily asked. She liked surprises.

"You'll see," Mom said. She winked at them.

Ben and Lily wondered what the surprise was. They hoped it was something fun and yummy. They walked faster on the path.

When they got to the store, Mom said, "Wait here for a minute. I'll be right back." She went inside the store.

Ben and Lily looked around. They saw a big truck with a picture of a clown on it. The truck had a sign that said, "Ice cream for sale."

"Look, Ben! Ice cream!" Lily said. She pointed at the truck.

"Wow! Ice cream!" Ben said. He loved ice cream.

They ran to the truck. The clown smiled at them and said, "Hello, kids. Do you want some ice cream?"

"Yes, please!" Ben and Lily said.

The clown gave them each a cone with a scoop of ice cream. Ben chose chocolate and Lily chose strawberry. They licked their ice cream and smiled.

"Thank you, clown!" Ben and Lily said.

"You're welcome, kids. Enjoy your ice cream," the clown said.

Mom came out of the store. She saw Ben and Lily with their ice cream. She smiled too.

"Did you like your surprise?" Mom asked.

"Yes, Mom! We love it!" Ben and Lily said.

They hugged Mom and said, "You're the best, Mom!"

Mom hugged them back and said, "You're the best, too, Ben and Lily!"

They walked back on the path, happy and full of ice cream. The path was not boring anymore. It was sweet and fun.

Sam and Tom are friends. They like to play in the street. They have cars and balls and bikes. But the street is dirty. There are papers and cans and bottles on the ground. Sam and Tom do not like the dirty street.

One day, Sam has an idea. He says to Tom, "Let's clean the street. We can use bags and gloves and brooms. We can make the street nice and shiny. Then we can play better."

Tom likes the idea. He says, "Yes, let's clean the street. We can be helpers. We can make the street happy."

Sam and Tom get their bags and gloves and brooms. They start to clean the street. They pick up the papers and cans and bottles. They sweep the dust and dirt. They work hard and fast.

But not everyone is happy. Ben and Jen are mean. They do not like to clean. They like to make messes. They see Sam and Tom cleaning the street. They laugh and shout, "Stop cleaning! You are silly! You are wasting your time! The street is always dirty. We like the dirty street. It is more fun."

Ben and Jen start to throw more papers and cans and bottles on the ground. They try to make the street dirty again. They try to stop Sam and Tom from cleaning.

Sam and Tom are sad and angry. They do not like Ben and Jen. They do not like their messes. They say, "Go away! You are mean! You are not helpers! You are making the street sad. We want to clean the street. We want to make the street nice and shiny. We want to play better."

Sam and Tom keep cleaning the street. They do not listen to Ben and Jen. They do not give up. They work harder and faster.

Soon, the street is clean. There are no papers and cans and bottles on the ground. There is no dust and dirt. The street is nice and shiny. Sam and Tom are happy. They say, "We did it! We cleaned the street. We are helpers. We are successful. The street is happy. We can play better."

Ben and Jen are not happy. They see the clean street. They see Sam and Tom smiling and playing. They feel bad. They say, "We are sorry. We were mean. We were not helpers. We were not successful. The street is not fun. We want to play better."

Sam and Tom are kind. They say, "It's okay. You can play with us. But you have to help us keep the street clean. You have to be helpers. You have to be successful. Then the street will be fun for everyone."

Ben and Jen agree. They say, "Yes, we will help you keep the street clean. We will be helpers. We will be successful. We want to have fun with everyone."

Sam and Tom, Ben and Jen, and the street are all happy. They play together in the clean street. They have cars and balls and bikes. They have fun. They are friends. The end.

Lily and Tom were playing with a big ball in the park. They liked to roll the ball to each other and catch it. Sometimes they rolled the ball very fast and far, and sometimes they rolled it very slow and near.

One day, a big dog came to the park. The dog saw the ball and wanted to play too. The dog ran to the ball and bit it with his teeth. The ball popped and made a loud noise. Lily and Tom were scared and sad. The dog had broken their ball.

"Hey, dog, that was our ball!" Tom shouted. "You are a bad dog! You made a waste of our ball!"

The dog barked and growled. He did not like Tom's words. He thought Tom was noisy and mean. He jumped on Tom and knocked him down. Tom cried and screamed. Lily ran to help Tom, but the dog was too big and strong.

A man came to the park and saw what was happening. He was the dog's owner. He called the dog and put a leash on him. He said sorry to Lily and Tom, but he did not give them a new ball. He took the dog and left the park.

Lily and Tom were hurt and angry. They had no ball and no fun. They went home and told their mom what happened. Their mom hugged them and gave them a cookie, but they were still not happy. They wished they had their ball back. They wished the dog had never come to the park. They wished they had a better day.

Tom and Sue were twins who liked to play all day. They had many toys and games, but they never wanted to stop and take a nap. Their mom always told them that naps were good for them, but they did not listen.

One day, mom said, "It is time for your nap, Tom and Sue. You have played enough. Go to your beds and sleep for a while."

Tom and Sue said, "No, mom, we do not want to nap. We want to play more. Please, mom, let us play."

Mom said, "No, you have to nap. You are restless and cranky. You need to rest your eyes and your brains. Go to your beds now, or you will be in trouble."

Tom and Sue did not like mom's words. They were angry and stubborn. They said, "Fine, mom, we will go to our beds, but we will not nap. We will quit playing, but we will not sleep."

They went to their beds, but they did not close their eyes. They whispered and giggled and made noises. They threw their pillows and blankets around. They did not care if mom heard them or not.

Mom heard them and was very upset. She went to their room and saw the mess they made. She said, "Tom and Sue, what are you doing? You are not napping at all. You are making a lot of noise and trouble. You are very naughty and rude. You have to clean up your room and say sorry to me. And you have to nap for an extra hour. No more playing for you today."

Tom and Sue were very sad and sorry. They wished they had listened to mom and napped when she told them to. They realized that naps were not so bad after all. They cleaned up their room and said sorry to mom. They lay down in their beds and tried to nap, but it was too late. They were not sleepy anymore. They lay awake and bored for a long time. They missed their toys and games. They had a bad day.

Sara and Ben were playing with their toys in the living room. They had a lot of fun making noises and pretending to be animals. But soon they got tired and wanted to rest.

"Let's go to my room and lie on the bed," Sara said. "We can read a book or watch a show."

"OK," Ben agreed. "But can we take some toys with us? I like to cuddle with them."

Sara nodded and picked up her favorite doll. Ben grabbed his toy truck and followed her. They went upstairs and opened the door to Sara's room.

But when they saw the room, they gasped. It was very messy and dirty. There were clothes, books, papers, and toys everywhere. And there was a lot of dust on the floor, the furniture, and the bed.

"Who made this mess?" Sara asked. "It was not like this when we left."

"I don't know," Ben said. "Maybe it was the wind. Or a monster."

Sara frowned. She did not like the wind or monsters. She did not like dust either. It made her sneeze and itch. She wanted to rest in a clean and cozy room.

"We have to clean this up," she said. "We can't rest here. It's too yucky."

Ben sighed. He did not like to clean. He liked to play. He wanted to rest with his toy truck. He thought cleaning was not useful.

"Do we have to?" he asked. "Can't we just go to your mom's room or the couch?"

"No, we can't," Sara said. "This is our room. We have to take care of it. And cleaning is useful. It makes things nice and neat. And it makes us happy."

Ben did not look happy. He looked sad and bored. He did not want to argue with Sara. He liked her. She was his friend. But he did not like cleaning. He thought it was hard and boring.

He looked at his toy truck. He wished he could play with it. He wished he could rest with it. He wished there was no dust. He wished there was no mess. He wished there was no cleaning. He wished there was only fun.

One day, they go to the park to play with bricks. They find a nice spot under a big tree. They start to build a big house with bricks. They are happy.

But then, a big dog comes. The dog is not obedient. The dog does not listen to his owner. The dog runs to Tom and Sam. The dog wants to play with bricks too. The dog knocks down the house with his paws. The dog barks and wags his tail.

Tom and Sam are sad and angry. They worked hard to build the house. They say to the dog, "Go away! These are our bricks! You are a bad dog!"

The owner of the dog comes. He sees the mess. He says to Tom and Sam, "I'm sorry. My dog is naughty. He likes to play with everything. He did not mean to ruin your house. Can you forgive him?"

Tom and Sam look at the dog. The dog looks sorry. He licks his lips and whines. Tom and Sam feel sorry for the dog. They say to the owner, "It's okay. We forgive him. But can you teach him to be obedient? He should not touch our bricks."

The owner nods. He says, "Yes, I will. Thank you for being kind. Do you want to play with my dog? He can fetch and roll over and sit. He is fun to play with."

Tom and Sam think for a moment. They like to play with animals. They say, "Okay. We will play with your dog. But first, can we rebuild our house?"

The owner smiles. He says, "Of course. I will help you. And I will watch my dog. He will not bother you again."

Tom and Sam smile too. They rebuild their house with bricks. They make it bigger and better. Then, they play with the dog. They throw a ball and he fetches it. They tell him to roll over and he does. They tell him to sit and he sits. He is obedient.

They have fun. They are friends. They share their bricks and their ball. They are happy.

"Hello, Mr. Snowman!" Lily said. "You are very lovely. Do you like your brush?"

The snowman did not say anything. He just smiled with his coal mouth.

Ben said, "Let's go inside and have some hot chocolate. It is very cold outside."

Lily nodded. She said, "Bye, Mr. Snowman. We will come back soon."

They ran inside the house and drank their hot chocolate. They felt warm and happy.

But outside, the sun was shining brighter and brighter. The snowman felt hot and wet. He started to melt.

"Oh no!" he thought. "I don't want to melt. I like my hat, my scarf, my carrot nose and my brush. I like Lily and Ben. They are very nice."

He wished he could go inside with them and have some hot chocolate too. But he could not move. He could only watch as his hat, his scarf, his carrot nose and his brush fell to the ground.

He felt very sad. He said, "Goodbye, Lily. Goodbye, Ben. Thank you for making me. You are very lovely."

Lily and Ben were twins who liked to play on the shore. They liked to dig in the sand, look for shells and splash in the water. One day, they saw a big boat with a flag and many people on it. They wondered what the boat was doing there.

"Let's go and see!" Ben said. He ran towards the boat, but Lily stopped him.

"Wait, Ben! We don't know who they are. They might be bad people. They might hurt us or take us away. We should stay here and tell Mom and Dad." Lily said.

"But I want to see the boat. It looks fun and mysterious. Maybe they have toys and candy. Maybe they want to be our friends." Ben said.

Lily shook her head. She did not understand why Ben was so curious and careless. She tried to pull him back, but he was too strong. He broke free and ran to the boat. Lily followed him, afraid and angry.

When they reached the boat, they saw a man with a big hat and a beard. He smiled and waved at them.

"Hello, little ones! Do you want to come aboard and see my boat? I have many things to show you. I am a pirate, and this is my pirate ship." He said.

Ben's eyes lit up. He liked pirates. He had a pirate hat and a pirate sword at home. He wanted to see the pirate ship. He nodded and climbed up the ladder.

Lily felt a chill in her heart. She did not like pirates. She had heard stories about pirates. They were mean and greedy. They stole and fought and lied. She did not want to see the pirate ship. She shook her head and stayed on the shore.

"Come on, Lily! Don't be scared. It's fun!" Ben called from the boat.

"No, Ben! Come back! It's not fun. It's dangerous. He is a bad man. He will trick you and hurt you. Please, come back!" Lily cried from the shore.

But Ben did not listen. He did not understand why Lily was so worried and boring. He followed the pirate man into the boat. He saw many things that made him happy. He saw gold and jewels and maps and guns. He saw a parrot and a monkey and a hook. He saw a big flag with a skull and bones.

The pirate man gave him a candy and a toy. He told him stories about his adventures and battles. He asked him if he wanted to be a pirate too. Ben said yes. He liked the pirate man. He thought he was his friend.

Lily waited on the shore. She waited and waited and waited. She hoped that Ben would come back soon. She hoped that he was safe and happy. She hoped that he would not forget her.

But Ben did not come back. He did not come back that day, or the next day, or the day after that. He did not come back ever. He stayed on the pirate ship. He became a pirate. He forgot about Lily. But Tim and Jen did not listen to the man. They thought he was a mean stranger who wanted to take their candy. They were ignorant of the danger. They said no to the man and ran away from him. They stayed near the rail and kept playing.

Lily and Ben like to fish with their dad. They have a big lake near their house. They have poles and hooks and worms. They catch fish and put them in a bucket.

One day, Lily and Ben see a furry animal near the lake. It has a long tail and a black mask. It is a raccoon. The raccoon is hungry and curious. It smells the fish in the bucket.

"Look, Ben, a raccoon!" Lily says. "It is so cute!"

"Be careful, Lily, it might bite!" Ben says. "Don't go near it!"

But Lily wants to pet the raccoon. She puts down her pole and walks slowly to the raccoon. The raccoon sees Lily and runs away. It knocks over the bucket and grabs a fish. It runs to the woods with the fish in its mouth.

"Oh no, the raccoon took our fish!" Ben says. "And look, Lily, you lost your pole!"

Lily looks at the lake and sees her pole floating away. She feels sad and sorry. She should have listened to Ben.

"Dad, dad, help!" Ben calls. "Lily lost her pole and the raccoon took our fish!"

Dad hears Ben and comes to the lake. He sees what happened. He hugs Lily and Ben and says, "Don't worry, kids, it's okay. We can get another fish and another pole. But next time, be careful with wild animals. They are not pets. They can be dangerous and sneaky."

Lily and Ben nod and say, "We're sorry, dad. We learned our lesson."

Dad smiles and says, "That's good. Now, let's go home and have some lunch. Maybe we can try fishing again another day."

Lily and Tom were friends who liked to play in the park. One day, they found a big cardboard box near the pond. They decided to make it into a boat and sail on the water.

They cut a hole in the box and put a stick and a sheet on it. They also found some grapes in Lily's bag and put them in the box. They were very happy with their boat and dragged it to the pond.

"Let's sail to the island!" Tom said, pointing to a patch of grass in the middle of the pond. "Maybe we can find treasure there!"

"Okay!" Lily said, climbing into the box. "But we have to be careful. The water is deep and the ducks are naughty. They might bite our boat."

They pushed the box into the water and used their hands to paddle. The boat moved slowly and wobbled a lot. The ducks saw them and swam towards them. They quacked loudly and pecked at the box.

"Go away, naughty ducks!" Tom shouted, waving his stick. "This is our boat, not yours!"

But the ducks did not listen. They kept pecking and quacking. One of them grabbed a grape from the box and ate it. Lily and Tom were very angry and scared. They wanted to go back to the shore, but the boat was leaking and sinking.

"Help! Help!" they cried, holding on to the box. "Our boat is broken and the ducks are mean!"

Some people on the shore heard them and came to help. They threw a rope to them and pulled them out of the water. They were wet and cold and sad. They hugged each other and thanked the people.

"Are you okay?" one of the people asked. "Why did you sail on the pond with a cardboard box?"

"We wanted to have fun and find treasure," Lily said, sniffing. "But the ducks were naughty and ate our grapes and broke our boat."

The people smiled and gave them some towels and cookies. They told them that sailing on the pond was not safe and that they should play somewhere else. They also told them that the ducks were not naughty, but hungry and curious.

Lily and Tom nodded and said sorry. They learned their lesson and promised to be more careful. They also gave some cookies to the ducks and made friends with them. They still liked to play in the park, but they never sailed on the pond again.

The mouse ran off and into the bushes. Sarah decided to grab the sack and chase after the mouse. She ran and ran, but the little mouse was too fast for her. Just then, Sarah tripped over a rock, and the mighty sack with her inside fell to the ground.

All of a sudden, Sarah saw the mouse peering out from the sack! She quickly untied the sack and let the mouse run off. She smiled and thought what a mighty adventure she had had!

"No, you miss, cowboy!" Lily said, dodging behind a tree. She threw an onion at Tom.

"Ow, that hurts!" Tom said, rubbing his head. "Why do you throw onions? They are boring and smelly!"

"Because they are fun and make you cry!" Lily said, laughing. She threw another onion at Tom.

Tom was angry. He ran after Lily with the toy gun. He wanted to shoot her back.

"Stop, stop, I give up, cowboy!" Lily said, seeing Tom coming. She dropped the onions and put her hands up.

"Too late, robber!" Tom said, shooting the toy gun. "Bang, bang, you are dead!"

Lily fell to the ground and pretended to be dead. She closed her eyes and stuck her tongue out.

Tom smiled. He had won the game. He went to Lily and poked her.

"Are you really dead, robber?" he asked.

Lily opened one eye and winked at Tom.

"No, I am not dead, cowboy," she said. "I am just joking. You are a good shooter."

Tom and Lily hugged and laughed. They decided to play something else. They left the toy gun and the onions in the garden. They were happy.

Tim has an idea. He goes to the kitchen and gets a toothpick. He pokes a hole in the book and takes out a small piece of the virus picture. He puts it in his mouth and bites it.

Tim makes a face. The virus picture does not taste like candy. It tastes like paper and ink and dirt. It is yucky. Tim spits it out and runs to the sink. He drinks some water and brushes his teeth.

Tim learns a lesson. He should not be so nosy and taste things that he does not know. He should ask his dad or mom first. He puts the book back in his dad's room and says sorry. "Look, I made a star!" Lily said, showing Ben her soap star.

"That's nice, but I can make a better shape," Ben said. He tried to make a car with the soap, but it was too hard. He had an idea. He put the soap in the microwave and turned it on.

"What are you doing?" Lily asked.

"I'm making the soap soft, so I can make a car," Ben said.

But the soap did not get soft. It got very hot and bubbly. It started to melt and make a mess in the microwave. The microwave made a loud noise and smoke came out.

"Uh-oh," Ben said.

Mom heard the noise and came to see what was wrong. She saw the melted soap and the smoke and was very angry.

"Ben, Lily, what did you do?" Mom asked.

"We wanted to play with soap," Lily said.

"That was very foolish," Mom said. "You could have hurt yourself or broken the microwave. Soap is not a toy. It is for washing. You need to clean up this mess and say sorry."

Ben and Lily felt bad. They said sorry to Mom and helped her clean up the melted soap. They learned their lesson and never played with soap again.

Tom and Mia were fish who lived in a big reef. They liked to swim and play with their friends. Sometimes they saw scary things, like sharks and eels, but they always stayed close to the reef where they were safe.

One day, Tom and Mia saw a big boat on the water. They were curious and wanted to see what it was. They swam closer and closer, until they saw a big net hanging from the boat. The net had many shiny things inside, like shells and coins and jewels.

"Wow, look at all those pretty things!" Mia said. "I want to touch them!"

"No, Mia, don't go near the net!" Tom said. "It might be a trap!"

But Mia did not listen. She swam towards the net and reached out her fin. As soon as she touched the net, it moved and closed around her. She was trapped!

"Help, help!" Mia cried. "Tom, save me!"

Tom was scared, but he loved Mia. He swam as fast as he could and bit the net with his teeth. He made a small hole and pulled Mia out. They swam away from the net and the boat.

"Thank you, Tom, you are my hero!" Mia said.

"I'm sorry, Tom, I was silly. I should have listened to you." Mia said.

"It's okay, Mia, I'm glad you are safe. Let's go back to the reef and wash ourselves. The net was dirty and smelly." Tom said.

They swam back to the reef and washed themselves with the clean water. They hugged each other and promised to never go near the boat again. They learned their lesson and lived happily in the reef.

The bird flew around the world. Everywhere it went, it felt the truth. It could feel that everything was right. It knew it was the most perfect bird!

Finally it came back to the same place it had started and saw the same wide sky again. It felt so proud - it had soared across the world. It spread its wings, flew up and soared happily ever after!

Once upon a time there was a lizard who was walking in a field. He was listening. "Crick-crack, crick-crack," the lizard heard. He looked around and saw a big bug. The bug was walking around the field. The lizard was very curious about where the bug was going. He followed the bug.

The bug scuttled up a tree and looked around. Then the bug peered down from the leaves at the lizard and said, "Would you like to come up here? I have a nice view." The lizard was very grateful and scurried up the tree.

He sat in the branches, listening to the bugs and birds all around. He heard the crickets still chirping, and the birds singing. He felt so happy and calm up in the tree.

The sun went down and the sky started to get dark. The lizard got ready to go home. He waved goodbye to the bug and thanked him for the nice view. Then he hopped away, listening to the night sounds.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Daisy. Daisy was three years old, and she loved to peek over the rail. She would stand on a chair and peer over the rail, looking down at the city below. 

One day, Daisy looked down and saw a gentle horse walking on the street. She wanted to pet the horse, but she knew she wasn't allowed to leave the house. So instead, she peeped over the rail, watching the horse walk away with its gentle gait. 

The next day, Daisy returned to the rail and peered down. Instead of a horse, she saw a cat. It was a cute little black and white kitty. Daisy wished she could climb down the rail and cuddle with the cat. 

But Daisy knew that she had to stay safe and stay inside. So she said goodbye to the cat, and she peeped over the rail one last time. 

Daisy had the best adventures without ever leaving the house. All she needed to do was peek over the rail.

"Hi, what are you reading?" a voice asked. Sara looked up and saw a boy standing in front of her. He had a friendly smile and a curious look.

The moral of the story is: Don't judge people by their appearance or preferences. Respect and appreciate their differences. Be kind and open-minded. You might find a friend.

"Thank you for telling the truth," she said. "But you have to learn from this mistake. You have to be gentle with books. And you have to share with each other. Books are for everyone to enjoy. Do you understand?"

The mama elephant was still mad, but then she decided to forgive her happy little elephant and gave him a big hug. From that day forward, the elephant reminded himself to always listen to his mama, even if it meant he couldn't change anything.

The sun was shining brightly one day and a little girl was out in the garden playing. She had a nice shiny pipe and pretended it was a magic wand. She ran around making funny noises, pretending to turn things into frogs and toadstools.

Suddenly she heard a strange sound. She stopped to see if it was coming from her pipe, but it wasn't. It came from above the garden. She looked up and saw a huge eagle. The eagle flew down and landed in front of the girl.

The eagle said: "I need your pipe. Please give it to me."
The girl was scared but eventually she decided to surrender the pipe to the giant eagle.

The eagle smiled and said: "Thank you. I wanted your pipe because I was looking for a way to help my babies. They were stuck in a tree and I couldn't reach them without your pipe. Now I can use it to help me rescue their little ones."

The little girl felt proud of herself. She had been brave and nice enough to lend her pipe and help the eagle.

Moral of the story: We should try to help others even if it takes us out of our comfort zone.

The man was confused and scared. He couldn't see anything outside except for a dark sky. He looked around and noticed that a huge monster was adding up the factory!

"You can swing later, but right now it's time to watch TV," said his mom.
