Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy was bald and loved to wear his favorite red hat. One day, Timmy's mom asked him to help her change a bulb in the lamp. Timmy didn't know what a bulb was, but he wanted to help his mom, so he said yes.

As they were changing the bulb, Timmy's mom said, "Timmy, did you know that when you grow up, you might lose all your hair and become bald like grandpa?" Timmy didn't like the sound of that, but he didn't say anything.

Later that day, Timmy went to visit his grandpa. When he saw his grandpa's bald head, he remembered what his mom had said earlier. Timmy looked up at his grandpa and said, "Grandpa, do you wear a hat like me because you don't have hair on your head?" Grandpa laughed and said, "Yes, Timmy, that's exactly why I wear a hat. Good observation!" Timmy smiled and felt proud of himself for figuring it out.

Tom got angry and said, "I don't need your corn! I am an independent man. I will grow my own corn and be rich like you!"

Once upon a time, there was a friendly sun. Every morning, the sun would shine bright and everyone was happy. 

One day, there were lots of clouds in the sky. The clouds were bossy, so they covered up the sun. Without the sun, everyone started to feel sad. 

The clouds wanted to help, so they included a rainbow in the sky. Everyone was so excited. Seeing the rainbow cheered them up. 

The rainbow made everyone happy again. The sun came back out and everyone danced and laughed. 

The clouds were happy that they had included the rainbow in the sky. They were no longer bossy. Now, whenever the sun is out, the clouds include a beautiful rainbow in the sky.

Once, there was a little girl named Jane. Every day, Jane would play in her backyard with her friends. She and her friends were very playful and always having so much fun. One day, she looked up and noticed dark clouds in the sky. She began to wonder what they could mean.

Soon, it started pouring rain. Jane and her friends ran inside to stay dry. But soon, the rain was coming down so hard, it was like a flood! Jane stood in her living room and watched as the water kept filling up the street outside. She wondered what would happen next.

Just then, something caught her eye - a duck swimming in the middle of the street! Jane and her friends watched in awe as the duck swam around and splashed in the water. It was playful and so much fun to watch!

But soon, the rain stopped and the water began to slowly drain away. Jane was sad that the flood had come and gone, but she was so happy to have seen the duck swimming around. From then on, she would always remember what a wonderful and interesting surprise the flood had been.

Once upon a time, there was a girl called Alice. She was very honest and was always looking for a secret. One day, she went for a walk in the forest.

Alice looked around, but she couldn't see any secrets. She said to herself, "Where is the secret?" She continued walking and looking until she found a little cave.

Alice went into the cave. She looked around and suddenly she saw it! It was a secret! It was a box with a bright blue bow on top.

Alice was very excited. She opened the box and there was a surprise inside. It was a toy!

Alice was so happy. She thanked the secret for finding such a nice surprise. She knew that she would always be honest and keep her secret.

There was once a little girl called Jenny. She was only three years old. She loved animals, especially lizards. One day, Jenny's parents took her to a zoo. As she walked around, she was amazed. Everything was so impressive! Everywhere she looked, there were animals. Then, suddenly, Jenny spotted something she hadn't seen before. It was a huge, green lizard. Jenny was so excited and clapped her hands. The lizard saw her and slowly crawled towards her. Jenny opened her arms and welcomed it. The lizard jumped on them and they spent the rest of the day together. It was an amazing and special moment for Jenny. She and the lizard were very happy.

Once upon a time, there was a happy little frog. He wanted to go for a swim. He hopped out of his pond and started to look for the perfect spot to dive in. He saw a big, white cloud in the sky and thought it was the perfect place.

The frog was a bit anxious. He was scared of getting wet. But his excitement was bigger than his fear, so he jumped into the cloud. He swam around in the cloud and felt so happy. It was so soft and fluffy.

Suddenly, it started to rain. The frog was even more anxious. He started to swim faster and faster looking for something to hold onto. Finally, he saw a leaf. He grabbed the leaf and held it tight.

The rain stopped and the sun came out. The frog let go of the leaf and it floated away. He was so happy to see the sun again. It was time to go home. He hopped back to his pond and had a good long rest.

Once there was a little boy called Bob who loved his wheel. It was round and shiny and had four spokes. He liked to match the different colours of the wheel. He would mix red, blue and yellow and he thought it was funny.

Bob liked to play with his wheel. He would run around and around, never stopping. He liked to make the wheel go faster and faster. One day Bob had an idea. He took his red, blue and yellow pieces and matched them to the spokes of his wheel.

When he was finished, Bob smiled at his creation. He thought it was the most fun thing he had ever done. He rolled the wheel around the room, colouring the walls with his fantastic creation. Bob was so proud of what he had done and he knew this was going to be his most favourite wheel ever!

Once upon a time, there was a rain. It was very mysterious. It came down from the sky and made everything wet. It was fun to play in.

One day a little girl named Lucy was playing outside when it started to rain. She looked up and smiled. Then she had an idea. She said, "I dare myself to run around in the rain!"

So she took off her shoes, rolled up her pants, and ran around and around. She spun in circles and laughed. She felt silly and free and happy.

The rain got harder and harder, but Lucy kept going. She kept running and spinning until her clothes were all wet and she was so tired she could hardly stand up. Then she collapsed in a heap and laughed until her stomach hurt.

When it was all over, she looked around. Everything was wet and sparkly and new. She knew she had been brave and that made her feel proud. That's how Lucy learned to dare.

Once upon a time, there was a little thing. It was small and round and orange. The thing was sour. Everyone didn't like it. They wanted to replace it with something sweeter.

Finally, the thing was gone. Now, there was a sweet, yummy thing in its place! Everyone smiled. It was a big, juicy apple!

They all started munching on the apple. It was so good! The sour thing was gone, and they were very happy.

The End!

Once upon a time, there was a little car. His handle was wet and broken. One day, he found a friend who said he could help fix it.

The friend had all the things he needed - a hammer, some glue, and some time! He helped the car make his handle better. They worked together for a long time, until the handle was nice and dry.

The car was so happy! He thanked his friend and said a big goodbye. Then he drove away with his new fixed handle. He was now able to go wherever he wanted!

Once there was a young girl named Cassie. She was 3 years old and loved to play.

One day, while playing in the park, Cassie saw something interesting. It was a small note lying on the ground. She picked it up and saw it said something sweet. It said "You are special".

Cassie felt so happy! She decided to keep the note and keep it in her pocket.

From then on, Cassie always carried the note with her. Whenever she felt down, the note would make her smile and feel sweet.

That's why Cassie loved her special note so much. It always made her feel better no matter what!

John was a very honest boy. He wanted to create something special. Every day he got an idea of a novel. One day, he decided to write down his ideas. He went to his room and took out some paper and pencils. He got to work, writing and drawing.

At first, it was hard for him. But he kept trying and soon he created a beautiful novel. He was so proud of his work. He showed it to his parents and they were very impressed.

John kept creating new and exciting stories. His parents were always so happy and proud to see what John could create. His honest and creative stories made everyone smile.
